I proto roste význam pravidelného školení zaměstnanců. O2 na to reaguje programem O2 Cyber Academy. Ten kombinuje krátká videa, simulované útoky, kvízy a vše průběžně vyhodnocuje.

items.title: Při léčbě rakoviny by mohly pomoct implantáty do mozku. Do startupu investuje i OpenAI

Mozkové implantáty se obecně přesouvají ze světa sci-fi do reality, jelikož technologičtí giganti jako OpenAI stále častěji investují do ambiciózních startupů, které je vytvářejí.

items.title: V Krkonoších přibývá pozorování kudlanky nábožné. Překvapující je nález z hrany Labského dolu ve výšce 1350 metrů
items.summary_raw: Správci Krkonošského národního parku (KRNAP) se díky spolupráci s veřejností letos dozvěděli o více než dvaceti pozorování teplomilné kudlanky nábožné v Krkonoších. Přestože většina jich byla z nižších a středních poloh ochranného pásma národního parku, tři nálezy jsou z míst nad hranicí 900 metrů nad mořem, informovali zástupci parku. Kudlanka nábožná je teplomilný dravý hmyz, který byl v Česku dříve typický jen pro jižní Moravu. Její šíření podle vědců souvisí se změnou klimatu.

Jde o evropsky významnou lokalitu a přírodní památku Orlice. Stavbaři v cenném mokřadním prostředí odtěží asi 4000 metrů krychlových sedimentů, udělají vegetační úpravy a obnoví vodní biotopy. Práce asi za osm milionů korun by měly být hotové na jaře 2028, uvedlo Povodí Labe.

items.title: Higher temperatures fuel gun violence. Now we know how much is from climate change.
items.summary_raw: This year, Philadelphia is on track to have the lowest number of homicides since 1963. But over Fourth of July weekend, a heat dome stretching from Maine to the Gulf of Mexico descended, leaving 165 million people facing major or extreme heat. Cities including Boston, Baltimore, and Raleigh saw record temperatures, and readings in Philadelphia topped 100 degrees for three consecutive days. The sweltering city also saw a busy weekend for gun violence. Between July 2 and July 4, the Gun Violence Archive recorded nine shootings, leaving three dead and nine wounded. “Those who commit gun violence are in a vulnerable population that have limited economic ability to make sure that they have air conditioning,” said Marion Campbell, executive director of Eddie’s House, a Philadelphia nonprofit that provides violence prevention and social services to such populations. “When you get hot you get irritated, OK! I’m just going to keep it real. You get irritated and your inability to manage your frustration could be heightened.” Research confirms what Campbell and others see on the ground: When temperatures rise, gun violence increases. What was previously unknown was the effect of climate change on gun violence. A new finding shared with The Trace by Climate Central, a nonprofit focused on climate change research and communication, estimates that approximately 2,000 shootings between 2021 and 2025 in the 100 U.S. cities with the most gun violence are attributable to high temperatures…

items.title: Češi za ojetiny platí přes 300 tisíc korun. Prodejci přitom často lžou o prvním majiteli

Dovoz ojetin ze zahraničí se zvýšil téměř o devět procent, nejprodávanějším modelem zůstává Škoda Octavia. Téměř u dvou třetin aut označených jako vozy po prvním majiteli jde podle společnosti Cebia o nepravdivý údaj.

Česko je až na chvostu unie. V přehledu ukazujeme deset evropských zemí, které na školství dávají vzhledem ke svému HDP nejméně.

items.title: Uplynulých sedm dní očima Ivana Lampera
Češi vzali útokem překvapivou evropskou destinaci. Zájem o ni vzrostl o 86 procent
items.summary_raw: Češi o podzimních prázdninách míří především za teplem, dvě třetiny cestujících volí jih Evropy. Letenky jsou oproti ročnímu průměru zhruba o pětinu dražší, výrazně roste zájem o Albánii, Egypt i exotické destinace. Zvýšený nápor očekávají také železniční dopravci, kteří posilují spoje do zahraničí a doporučují včasný nákup jízdenek.

items.title: Brusel chce děti odstřihnout od sítí. Nepomůže to, varuje poradce Komise EU
items.summary_raw: Evropská komise chce omezit přístup dětí k sociálním sítím. Návrh ale vyvolává kritiku kvůli ochraně osobních údajů i snadnému obcházení zákazů. Podle odborníků navíc opomíjí důležitost digitálního vzdělávání.

items.title: Kolínské muzeum otevře výstavu o životě a odkazu svatého Vojtěcha, představí malbu z počátku 16. století
items.summary_raw: Na výstavě věnované svatému Vojtěchovi představí Regionální muzeum v Kolíně mimo jiné oltářní desku z počátku 16. století, na které je světec vyobrazen společně s Janem Husem. Návštěvníci uvidí také model sochy svatého Vojtěcha pro Karlův most od Ferdinanda Maxmiliána Brokoffa.

items.title: Ukrajinské drony zabily v ruské příhraniční oblasti tři lidi, další zranily
items.summary_raw: Ukrajinské drony útočily v noci na neděli na ruské území. Útok v Belgorodské oblasti zabil tři lidi, nálet na průmyslový podnik v Permském kraji zase zranil pět zaměstnanců.

items.title: Amid Iowa’s Water Crisis, Factory Farms Get a Pass on Environmental Permitting

ESTHERVILLE, Iowa—By the time rainwater rolled down the hillside and reached the stream near the edge of Gordon Garrison’s property, it had turned a foul, murky red. Gravity had acted predictably, Garrison knew. […]
authors: Story by Anika Jane Beamer, photos by Zach Spindler-Krage

items.title: Na Wall Street se vrací nástroj z finanční krize 2008. Investoři se připravují na možný krach
items.summary_raw: Na amerických trzích prudce roste zájem o pojištění proti bankrotu technologických firem, investoři se obávají rizik spojených s boomem umělé inteligence. Objem obchodů s úvěrovými swapy u vybraných technologických gigantů vzrostl během dvou měsíců z méně než dvou na devět miliard dolarů týdně. Na finanční trhy se vracejí nástroje známé z krize v roce 2008 a sílí obavy, že masivní investice do AI mohou vyvolat další otřesy, píše businessový newsletter 11am.

items.title: Soudruh mi rval šňůry z mixpultu aneb Poklad po prastrýci
items.summary_raw: Světlo světa spatřil v milionářské vile, která ovšem jejich rodině nepatřila. Po únoru 1948 jí nepatřilo nic. V jedenácti letech přišel o matku, otec strávil v 50. letech dva roky v neblaze proslulé uherskohradišťské věznici. Neochota vstoupit do KSČ mu otevřela cestu ke splnění snu – živit se bigbítem, a to jako profesionální zvukař. Karel Popelka se stal nedílnou součástí nejen brněnské bigbítové a později i folkové scény 80. a počátku 90. let.

items.title: Sprosté básně i bratrovražedné války. Výstava v Brně přibližuje život moravských Lucemburků
items.summary_raw: Karla IV. zná každý podobně jako jezdeckou sochu jeho synovce Jošta v Brně. Už méně je v povědomí jejich příbuzný Jan Jindřich, který výrazně ovlivnil dějiny Moravy. Právě moravským Lucemburkům se věnuje výstava v Moravském zemském archivu v Brně. Návštěvníci na ní mohou vidět vzácné rukopisy, listiny a artefakty.

items.title: Blackout nezačíná tmou. Začíná tím, že nelze zaplatit, zavolat ani natankovat. Plus Grolich, Havlíček a český top byznys na Fóru HN
items.summary_raw: Velké celodenní byznysové Fórum Hospodářských novin na téma Bezpečnost, odolnost a byznys se koná už v úterý 3. listopadu v Rudolfinu. Soustředíme se na aktuální témata z pohledu českých firem a celé tuzemské ekonomiky. Mezi speakery a hosty jsou...

items.title: Sněžku bičuje orkán, na vrcholu je jako v Arktidě. Lanovka kvůli větru nepojede
items.summary_raw: Sněžku zasáhl vítr o síle orkánu, jehož nárazy přesáhly rychlost 141 kilometrů za hodinu. Kvůli extrémnímu počasí nepojede celý den horní úsek lanovky, turistům navíc hrozí nebezpečí na zledovatělých cestách. Silný vítr a déšť zasáhnou i další části Česka, ve vyšších horských polohách se očekává sněžení.

items.title: Volkswagen chce zmrazit mzdy ve Škodovce. Jeho Audi přitom postaví v USA továrnu za 91 miliard
items.summary_raw: Německá automobilka Audi postaví v americké Georgii továrnu za 91 miliard korun, která vytvoří přibližně 4 500 pracovních míst. Donald Trump označuje investici za úspěch své celní politiky, zatímco mateřský Volkswagen plánuje rozsáhlé propouštění. Koncern chce do konce desetiletí zrušit až 100 tisíc pracovních míst a podle odborů požaduje také zmrazení mezd ve Škodě Auto.

items.title: Národní park Šumava školí 25 nových průvodců. Detailně poznají i divočinu Bavorského lesa
items.summary_raw: Na Horské Kvildě probíhá historicky první školení nových průvodců přírodou a krajinou Šumavy a Bavorského lesa. Na každé straně hranice se do něj zapojí 25 účastníků. Mezi Čechy byl zájem výrazně vyšší. Certifikovanými průvodci se stanou za dva roky. „Poptávka po průvodcích roste ze strany skupin i jednotlivců,“ říká pro Český rozhlas Plzeň koordinátor školení Josef Štenberk.

items.title: Rekordní sazby tankerů tlačí cenu ropy a paliv dále vzhůru
items.summary_raw: Cena samotné ropy tvoří pouze část koncové ceny barelu. Podle nové analýzy Mezinárodní energetické agentury (IEA) vystřelily sazby za tankerovou přepravu v září na historická maxima. Zdražují tak dodávky ropy i paliv po celém světě a postupně se promítají i do cen pro spotřebitele. Přeprava tvoří obvykle jen malý díl konečné ceny ropy. Když se […]

items.title: Liberecký kraj vytipoval 55 lokalit napříč regionem, které jsou nejvíc ohroženy erozí zemědělské půdy
items.summary_raw: Šedesát procent zemědělské půdy v Česku je podle analýzy Výzkumného ústavu meliorací a ochrany půdy ohroženo erozí. V Libereckém kraji se to týká zejména oblastí na Českolipsku a Semilsku. Kraj už vytipoval 55 lokalit, kde je situace nejhorší. A pracovníci výzkumného ústavu je teď dopodrobna mapují.

items.title: Chorvatsko už nebude pro každého. Mění se v destinaci bohatých, říká český developer
items.summary_raw: Chorvatsko se podle zakladatele Domoplanu Tomáše Vavříka postupně mění z dostupné dovolenkové destinace na luxusní lokalitu. Developerská skupina v zemi rozvíjí rozsáhlý resort a založila samostatný investiční fond zaměřený na chorvatské nemovitosti. Vavřík očekává další růst cen nemovitostí také v Česku, zejména kvůli nedostatečné výstavbě a vysoké poptávce.

items.title: Reportáž z čínské továrny: Takhle vzniká něco mnohem většího než jen postrach Volkswagenu
items.summary_raw: Čína nepředhání evropské automobilky, staví mnohem širší produkt kombinující fyzický svět, nenahmatatelnou AI a mix wow efektu s latentně děsivým dojmem. Auto už nestojí v centru pozornosti, je pouze jednou z mnoha odnoží ekosystému, stejně jako roboti, humanoidi, vznášedla nebo zemědělská technika. Alespoň takový obraz budoucnosti kreslí hostům týdne „otevřených dveří“ čínská automobilka Chery doma ve Wu-chu, odkud pochází i reportáž e15.

items.title: Kulturní impérium Jakuba Havrlanta a Karla Komárka roste. V zákulisí už probíhají změny
items.summary_raw: Jakub Havrlant a Karel Komárek stále víc propojují prostřednictvím společnosti Rockaway Arts tři významné české festivaly. Karlovarský filmový festival, Colours of Ostrava a Designblok začínají sdílet týmy, zkušenosti i kontakty. Designblok nově využívá tým karlovarského festivalu pro péči o VIP hosty. Díky silnějšímu zázemí rozšířil tým, získal nové partnery a chystá zahraniční expanzi.

items.title: Jana Patková: Pomoc kočkám nesmí být otázkou štěstí. Pirátský pozměňovací návrh jim má zajistit lepší život
items.summary_raw: Na mnoha místech Česka se kočky nekontrolovaně množí a bez potřebné péče trpí hladem, nemocemi a zraněními. Zatímco některé obce zajišťují kastrace a veterinární péči, jiné před problémem zavírají oči. V jedné obci tak kočka dostane pomoc, zatímco o pár kilometrů dál zůstane odkázaná na dobrovolníky a útulky. Opravdu má o životě kočky rozhodovat to, ve které obci se narodila?

items.title: Eva Ješutová: Pásek s Dubčekovým projevem mohl skončit smazaný. Zachránil ho rozhlasový archiv
items.summary_raw: Čerstvá členka rozhlasové Síně slávy Eva Ješutová nastoupila do Českého rozhlasu v roce 1981 a o šest let později se stala vedoucí archivu. Zažila proměnu archivářské práce od kartoték až po digitální záznamy a podílela se na uchování unikátních historických nahrávek. Jednou z nich byl i dosud neidentifikovaný pásek s projevem Alexandra Dubčeka po návratu z Moskvy v roce 1968. Rozhlasový archiv pomohl také Jiřímu Mádlovi při přípravě filmu Vlny.

items.title: Noční útok na veřejnoprávní média je přímým ohrožením demokracie
items.summary_raw: Krajní pravice, má-li si udržet moc, potřebuje změnit podmínky politické soutěže tak, aby ji strukturálně zvýhodňovaly. Veřejnoprávní média lze hájit, aniž by se přitom rezignovalo na kritiku některých jejich nepřijatelných stránek.

items.title: Zandl a Koubský: Dosáhnout záruky, že AI nezneužijí špatní lidé, je iluzorní. Džin je venku z lahve
items.summary_raw: Umělá inteligence možná už za několik let vyhubí lidstvo a je potřeba zpomalit její vývoj. Podobná prohlášení zazněla i od šéfů dvou největších vývojářských studií, OpenAI a Anthropic. „AI umí dát i nepříliš chytrým lidem velmi chytré postupy, to je ta nebezpečná změna,“ vysvětluje publicista a provozovatel webu Vibecoding.cz Patrick Zandl. „Dosáhnout vysoké záruky, že to nezneužijí špatní lidé, je iluzorní,“ říká redaktor Deníku N Petr Koubský.

items.title: Francii zachvátila nová vlna protestů. Do ulic vyšly všechny generace, policie nasadila vodní děla
items.summary_raw: Francií zmítá další vlna protestů proti vládě, do ulic vycházejí lidé všech generací. V Paříži podle odborů demonstrovalo 250 tisíc lidí navzdory dešti a vládním omezením. Demonstrace přerostly v násilné střety s policií, která nasadila vodní děla a slzný plyn.

items.title: Třebíčské muzeum se věnuje lokalitě zaplavené Dalešickou přehradou
items.summary_raw: Muzeum Vysočiny Třebíč (MVT) připravilo akce věnované historii území zaplaveného Dalešickou přehradou. Na mapování osudů zaniklých obcí, mlýnů a osad v údolí řeky Jihlavy, které zmizely kvůli stavbě přehrad a Jaderné elektrárny Dukovany, pracuje MVT s Akademií věd.

items.title: Hlasatel BBC, zpravodajec i odborář. Student získal ocenění za zmapování osudů Josefa Kosiny
items.summary_raw: Ceny Edvarda Beneše oceňují studentské historické práce zaměřené na dějiny 20. století. Předávaly se v Sezimově Ústí a mezi oceněnými byl také čtyřiadvacetiletý student Masarykovy Univerzity Michal Holub z Opočna. Ve své diplomové práci se věnoval Josefu Kosinovi, dalšímu rodákovi z Opočna a hlasateli BBC za druhé světové války. „Kosina byl osobnost, která si určitě zaslouží naši pozornost,“ říká v rozhovoru pro Český rozhlas Hradec Králové.

items.title: Olomoucká botanická zahrada zachraňuje zvonovec liliolistý, daří se množit
items.summary_raw: Vzácný zvonovec liliolistý, který během 20. století zmizel z většiny svých původních lokalit v České republice, se daří rozmnožovat v Botanické zahradě Přírodovědecké fakulty Univerzity Palackého v Olomouci (PřF UP). Ze semen pocházejících z přírodní památky Vražba v Královéhradeckém kraji zde vyrostly nové rostliny, které pomohou posílit jeho oslabené populace ve volné přírodě. Přibližně polovina semenáčků se na začátku října vrátila na přírodní stanoviště, sdělili ČTK zástupci fakulty.

items.title: Premiér přirovnal protesty proti rušení poplatků pro veřejnoprávní média k útoku na Kapitol
items.summary_raw: Co se vlastně dělo před sněmovnou během pátečního nočního vládního útoku na televizi a rozhlas

items.title: V Kodani se objevily kontejnery na použité pleny, budou se recyklovat
items.summary_raw: Komunální služby v Kodani začaly s rozmisťováním nových kontejnerů na třídění použitých plen, které zamíří k recyklaci do speciálního zařízení na jihozápadním předměstí dánské metropole. Vedení města tak chce omezit spalování odpadu.

items.title: Hradec Králové má studii Central parku o 84 hektarech, vybuduje jej postupně
items.summary_raw: Město Hradec Králové má hotovou urbanisticko-krajinářskou studii na vybudování takzvaného Central parku v jižní části města. Území o rozloze 84 hektarů navazuje na největší hradecké panelové sídliště Moravské Předměstí. Město chce park budovat postupně. Prvním již hotovým prvkem je nedávná obnova historického schodiště na Kopec sv. Jana, uvedla radnice. Studii pro město udělalo sdružení brněnských architektů Lucie Radilové a Zdeňka Sendlera.

items.title: Zlínská zoo letos odchovala mláďata ptáků, u kterých je rozmnožování vzácné
items.summary_raw: Zlínská zoo letos odchovala mláďata ptačích druhů turako velký, vousák velký a tukan obrovský, jejichž rozmnožování je v lidské péči vzácné. Vyžaduje velké zkušenosti a odborné znalosti chovatelského týmu, je to skutečně světový úspěch, sdělila ČTK mluvčí zahrady Romana Mikešová. Podle ní museli chovatelé u jednotlivých druhů zvládnout zcela odlišné nároky, od specifické výživy přes složité partnerské soužití až po správně načasovanou péči o vejce a mláďata.

items.title: Vojenské lesy otevřely na Doupově v Javorné areál pro ekologický chov skotu
items.summary_raw: Areál pro ekologický chov skotu s moderními technologiemi otevřeli v Javorné na Karlovarsku Vojenské lesy a statky (VLS.) Součástí automatizovaného kravína pro odchov mladého dobytka je i zázemí pro mobilní jatka, informoval ředitel státního podniku VLS Petr Král. Na projektu spolupracovaly VLS s armádou.

items.title: Geopolitical risk and energy poverty in African net energy importers: Localized effects, structural vulnerability, and conditional resilience
Forging holistic nuclear governance: The unifying role of China's atomic energy law in risk regulation and industry promotion
Zatopená Dolní Vltavice stále přitahuje dál pozornost veřejnosti i odborníků, nyní se k ní ponořil i spisovatel Štifter
items.summary_raw: Zatopená obec Dolní Vltavice na Českokrumlovsku jako silné memento komplikovaných dějin 20. století přitahuje dál pozornost veřejnosti i odborníků. Dnes se k ní ponořil také spisovatel Jan Štifter, který obci věnoval svůj nejnovější román. Zbytky obce odkryté díky poklesu hladiny lipenské přehrady nedávno zaměstnaly také historiky. Regionální muzeum v Českém Krumlově v uplynulém týdnu dokončilo přesun více než 90 náhrobních kamenů, které byly pod vodou přibližně od roku 1958, řekl ČTK ředitel muzea Martin Nechvíle.

items.title: Co prozradí ptačí zpěv a ultrazvuk netopýrů? Záznamy z milovické rezervace pomáhají luštit vědci v Dánsku
items.summary_raw: Dlouhodobě sledovat ptáky a netopýry v milovické rezervaci ve Středočeském kraji pomáhají vědcům z Agentury ochrany přírody a krajiny akustické nahrávače. Zařízení připevněná na stromech zachycují ptačí zpěv i ultrazvuk netopýrů, který lidské ucho neslyší. Nahrávky pak putují do Dánska, kde je odborníci vyhodnocují pomocí umělé inteligence.

items.title: Ultrychytrý AI zubní kartáček s kamerou za 11 tisíc korun od slavného výrobce. Co by se mohlo pokazit...

For Black voters, climate action means little without relief from rising costs
items.summary_raw: For Elijah Lee, protecting the environment has always been about what’s happening close to home. He grew up in a predominantly Black, low-income community in Roanoke Rapids, North Carolina, and went to school next to a paper mill that filled the air with pollution. He always wondered why it seemed like the only employment option for people in town. Now, as data centers expand in Virginia, where he moved as a teenager, he fears the political promises of data center-driven economic growth won’t reach him or his generation. At 18, Lee is preparing to vote in his first midterm election. Climate policy ranks among his top concerns. But he understands why people struggling to pay their bills might not put it first. “It’s hard to care about the quality of your air or your food that you eat and whether or not that food is actually clean when you can’t even afford the food in the first place,” he said. New polling suggests that tension is widespread. Black voters may not name climate change as their biggest election concern, but they still want leaders to address it. items.title: Provenance-audited retrieval-augmented generation for national adaptation reporting: a computer-science evaluation of citation-fabrication risk in climate analytics pipelines
items.source_name: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
items.summary_raw: National adaptation reporting under the Paris Agreement requires climate-analytics pipelines that can trace every quantitative claim to a verifiable source. Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) offers a way to ground narrative synthesis in a document corpus, but its citation behaviour under adversarial or sparse retrieval conditions remains uncharacterised. The framework defines a provenance graph over retrieved passages and generated claims, and introduces a fabrication-risk score that combines retrieval coverage, citation-claim entailment probability, and source-identity stability. A replication-based evaluation across 1,000 computed reporting tasks shows that fabrication risk rises sharply when retrieval coverage falls below 0.6 and when the corpus contains near-duplicate documents with conflicting metadata. The analysis identifies a coverage–fabrication trade-off that is invisible to standard RAG evaluation metrics such as answer accuracy or BLEU. The contribution is a formal, auditable risk model that national reporting teams can apply before deploying RAG in adaptation-pipeline workflows.

items.title: Drivers of supply chain resilience in the new energy vehicle industry: An explainable machine learning approach
items.summary_raw: Under the global dual-carbon goals, supply chain resilience has become a strategic priority for the new energy vehicle (NEV) industry. Using a 2016–2023 panel of 403 Chinese listed NEV firms, we construct an entropy-weighted supply chain resilience index and predict it with Random Forest (RF) and XGBoost, interpreted via SHAP, against a linear regression benchmark. The tree-based ensembles explain 66%–68% of out-of-sample resilience variation, far above the linear benchmark (56%), while models using only supply chain characteristics fail to beat the sample mean. The two ensembles attribute resilience differently: transaction costs rank as the strongest supply chain predictor in RF, whereas chip import dependence dominates in XGBoost, though both agree that supply chain characteristics are stably among the top predictor groups. All five core factors exhibit nonlinear threshold patterns (on the normalized [0, 1] scale): automation first suppresses and then promotes resilience beyond a robot-penetration threshold of 0.19; government subsidies are effective mainly within an intensity window of 0.2–0.5; chip import dependence turns sharply detrimental beyond 0.77; innovation efficiency supports resilience only within an optimal moderate range, its contribution turning negative beyond 0.33; and transaction costs become resilience-enhancing only beyond thresholds of 0.15 (RF) to 0.21 (XGBoost). This study evaluates the role of participatory agricultural extension in addressing the adverse impacts of climate change on agricultural production from farmers` perspective. The findings revealed a limited implementation of participatory agricultural extension within agricultural extension centers in the centers in the study area, with 56.3% of respondents reporting low levels of participatory communication. Correlation analyses (Pearson and spearman) indicate significant negative relationships between participatory agricultural extension and farmers` age, education level, farm size, farm type, farming experience. Significant positive relationships were found with educational level, participation in training programs, and level of communication with information sources. items.title: Climate Change as a Stress Test for Public Governance
items.source_name: Uluslararası sosyal, siyasal ve mali araştırmalar dergisi.
items.summary_raw: This study conceptualizes climate change as a stress test for public governance systems. Moving beyond technological and informational explanations, it examines how institutional design, coordination mechanisms, digital governance tools, and participatory processes shape climate policy implementation. The article uses a structured narrative literature review with systematic search, screening, and thematic synthesis steps, drawing on peer-reviewed studies, academic books/book chapters, working papers, and leading institutional reports. Findings show that persistent implementation gaps stem primarily from weak governance capacity, even where formal strategies and commitments exist. Core barriers include limited vertical and horizontal coordination, institutional fragmentation, low policy coherence, weak governance of digital tools, and under-institutionalized participation. The “stress test” metaphor is used analytically to show how climate change reveals structural vulnerabilities in governance systems. The study concludes that durable climate action requires long-term investment in governance reforms: strengthened coordination, closer integration of policy and budgeting frameworks, accountable governance of digital infrastructures, and institutionalized participation.

items.title: The Impact of Heatwave Exposure and Climate Change on Maternal Health and Pregnancy Outcomes: A Public Health Review
items.summary_raw: Background: Climate change is increasing the frequency, intensity, and duration of extreme heat events. Pregnancy is a heat-vulnerable physiological state because maternal cardiovascular, metabolic, and thermoregulatory demands rise while fetal development depends on stable uteroplacental function. Purpose: This review synthesizes evidence on heatwave exposure, maternal health, pregnancy outcomes, biological pathways, vulnerable populations, and public-health responses. Methods: A narrative public-health review was conducted using peer-reviewed systematic reviews, meta-analyses, cohort studies, and authoritative guidance, with emphasis on evidence published from 2020 to 2025 while retaining selected earlier landmark studies. Results: The strongest and most consistent evidence concerns preterm birth. A 2025 meta-analysis of 198 studies from 66 countries reported higher odds of preterm birth with increasing heat exposure and during heatwaves. Evidence also links heat with low birth weight, stillbirth, gestational diabetes, hypertensive disorders, placental complications, and selected congenital anomalies, although effect sizes and certainty vary by outcome. Proposed pathways include dehydration, cardiovascular strain, altered uteroplacental perfusion, inflammation, oxidative stress, endocrine responses, and placental dysfunction. Social disadvantage, outdoor work, poor housing, and limited access to cooling may amplify risk. Conclusion: Extreme heat should be incorporated into…

items.title: Beliefs About Public Opinion and the Perceived Legitimacy of Policy Decisions
items.summary_raw: Abstract Democratic legitimacy is typically thought to depend on whether political decisions reflect public opinion, or majority preferences. Do citizens share this standard? And what if citizens are wrong about public opinion? We study how beliefs about public support for controversial policy proposals are associated with the perceived legitimacy of adopting them, and whether accurate polling information changes these judgments. In a representative survey experiment in Germany, respondents reported their own position on four such proposals, estimated public support, and rated the legitimacy of adopting each one. For a random subset of proposals, respondents received accurate polling information showing that the proposal lacked majority support. We find that perceived public support predicts legitimacy judgments even after accounting for respondents’ own policy preferences. Yet these perceptions are often inaccurate and shaped by respondents’ own views. Corrective polling information modestly lowers perceived legitimacy, especially among those who initially overestimated public support. The findings suggest that misperceptions of public opinion can distort, but accurate information can also partly correct, citizens’ assessments of democratic legitimacy.

items.title: Bridging the knowledge gap: assessing Nigerian construction professionals' awareness and readiness for zero-carbon initiatives
items.source_name: Built Environment Project and Asset Management
items.summary_raw: Purpose The built environment is a major contributor to global carbon emissions, making the transition to zero-carbon buildings essential. Achieving this transition depends on construction professionals' awareness and readiness to implement zero-carbon initiatives (ZCIs). However, empirical evidence on their preparedness in the Nigerian construction industry remains limited. This study assesses Nigerian construction professionals' knowledge and awareness of ZCIs supporting the zero-carbon transition. Design/methodology/approach A quantitative research design was adopted using a structured questionnaire administered to 225 Nigerian construction professionals. The questionnaire was validated through expert review and pilot testing. Purposive sampling was used to ensure representation of key industry stakeholders, and data were subsequently analyzed using descriptive statistical techniques. Findings The results reveal substantial awareness and capacity gaps among Nigerian construction professionals. Awareness of international climate agreements, national climate policies, and industry-led ZCIs was generally low. Familiarity, experience, and training in carbon assessment, building performance assessment, life cycle assessment, and energy modelling were also limited. These deficiencies indicate inadequate sectoral preparedness for the effective implementation of ZCIs in Nigeria's construction industry. items.title: Assessing the impacts of scientific theatre on the audience
items.summary_raw: Climate change communication aims to enhance climate literacy, strengthen public engagement, and foster attitudinal and behavioural change. Yet, its effects are rarely evaluated in a systematic way. This study applies a mixed-methods approach to assess the impacts of an arts-based activity on the audience using a combination of surveys and post-performance debates. Surveys conducted with secondary school students reveal the need to reinforce climate literacy within educational contexts. In addition, post-rehearsal feedback enabled the co-creation team of climate scientists, social scientists and playwrights and stage directors to introduce adjustments before the premiere, improving audience understanding. Finally, changes in audience learning, attitudes, and satisfaction were assessed, with findings showing increased understanding of climate change, trust in climate science, and interest in individual and collective pro-environmental attitudes. Although further analyses across broader population groups are needed, results suggest that arts-based approaches can facilitate the communication of complex climate concepts, enhancing emotional engagement and impact on the general public. It also shows that systematically evaluating communication interventions is key to determining whether the goals of communication actions are met.

items.title: Understanding public support for carbon capture, utilization and storage: The role of fairness perception
Measuring Biofuels Acceptance in the Transportation Sector in Indonesia: Public Knowledge, Attitudes and Perception
items.summary_raw: Greenhouse gas emissions are a major contributor to climate change, which originate from several sectors, including energy, transportation, manufacturing, and construction. However, the transportation sector accounts for approximately 25% of total emissions, indicating the urgent need for effective mitigation strategies. One potential solution is the use of renewable energy, particularly biofuels, which can reduce carbon dioxide emissions by partially replacing fossil fuels. In Indonesia, this transition is supported by Government Regulation No. 79/2014 on the National Energy Policy, including the mandatory B20 program that promotes biodiesel blending. Therefore, this study aims to examine public knowledge, attitudes, and perceptions regarding biofuel use in the transportation sector in Indonesia. Data were collected through a questionnaire survey involving 256 respondents and analyzed using analysis of variance (ANOVA) to assess differences across demographic factors. The results showed that respondents under 18 years of age had knowledge levels comparable to those aged 18–24, while significant differences were observed among older age groups. items.title: Social and psychological factors shaping public views of unconventional climate advocates
items.summary_raw: Abstract Climate communication faces a messenger challenge: while the urgency of climate crisis demands broad-based public engagement, conventional advocates who are left-leaning environmentalists often struggle to reach diverse audiences due to identity-based barriers and negative stereotypes. This study examines “unconventional advocates”: individuals or groups who advocate for climate action from within social identities not typically associated with environmentalism. Through public intercept interviews with 90 Australians across urban and regional areas, we identified five interrelated social and psychological factors shaping public evaluations of these atypical climate messengers: identification, surprise, group importance, trustworthiness, and legitimacy. Our findings reveal that public views of unconventional advocates are shaped not only by identity alignment, but also by broader stereotype-based expectations, perceived credibility and legitimacy, and the wider socio-political meanings attached to different groups. These findings advance theoretical understandings of social identity, impression formation, and climate communication, while informing practical strategies in climate advocacy to broaden the social base of support for climate action.

items.title: The planet’s vital signs are getting worse. One of the easiest fixes is your diet.
items.summary_raw: A new report examining more than a dozen of the Earth’s life-sustaining systems paints a pretty bleak picture. Published last week in BioScience, the seventh annual State of the Climate report shows how global warming is producing significant shifts in the planet’s overall health and destabilizing the climate as a whole. Key climate indicators are going in the wrong direction: greenhouse gas emissions, sea level rise, glacier thickness, ice mass, and more. These shifts should no longer be taken as warning signs about some distant future, the authors write; instead, they amount to a “diagnosis” of how climate change is impacting the planet today — and where things will go if human behavior doesn’t change quickly or sufficiently enough. Concentrations of carbon dioxide, methane , and nitrous oxide, stemming primarily from the burning of fossil fuels, hit record highs this year. Meanwhile, glacier thickness and Greenland ice mass are at record lows. Things are also not looking good for the Earth’s energy imbalance, a measure of how much energy the planet absorbs from the sun versus how much of that energy exits the atmosphere. This measure has been rising , a sign of how the planet, essentially, is heating up. Of the 16 climate indicators examined by the authors, seven — or 44 percent — are at record extremes. The paper also discusses worrisome feedback loops, or how existing warming might be further accelerated by phenomena like wildfires or permafrost melting that release…

items.summary_raw: This week’s conversation is with Leah Qusba, CEO of GoodPower, which recently released a survey experiment you need to read. Conducted with Data for Progress, the project, published Monday, takes a unique approach to asking people why they opposed data centers for artificial intelligence and whether constructing renewable energy instead of gas power moves the needle at all in their support for AI infrastructure near them. Instead of just asking polling questions, they posed various hypothetical project designs to people — and the results were eye-popping. Turning to solar instead of gas? Might not be a panacea for gaining approval at the local level. Protecting electricity rates from going sky-high? Now that’s a way to get buy-in. The following conversation was lightly edited for clarity. Before we jump into the survey, is the data center boom changing the trajectory for renewable energy development in the U.S.? If you look back over the last decade and a half, the largest global procurer of decarbonized electricity has been the Big Tech industry. I think we’re still seeing the trendlines of that today. items.title: A First-Of-Its-Kind State of Emergency — Over a Permitting Pause
items.summary_raw: 1. Umatilla County, Oregon – A small town in Oregon this week declared a state of emergency over fears that a statewide pause on data center permits will harm its economy. Five of the six people on the Umatilla city council voted to adopt a resolution formally calling for a state of emergency “due to the threat of widespread financial loss.” Umatilla City Manager Dave Stockdale told the council before the vote that the data center pause enacted by Governor Tina Kotek puts millions in tax revenue at risk. Other city staffers told the council that current budget reserves are healthy, but this could complicate a bond for a new police station and delay executing their city’s master plan. Umatilla is home to more than 20 data center projects currently operating or under development, equal to roughly one-fifth of the state’s data center sector. Oregon law expressly grants cities and towns permission to declare a state of emergency over “financial loss.” And the Umatilla resolution is a clear legal threat; its text calls for “immediate reconsideration” of Governor Kotek’s directive pausing data center permits and “authorizes the city manager to coordinate with affected governments and legal counsel to pursue appropriate administrative and judicial remedies.” To the best of our knowledge, this is the first time a municipal government has threatened legal action or declared a state of emergency over a state-wide permitting pause against data center development. items.title: The Most Important Data Center Election You’ve Never Heard Of
items.summary_raw: An election-season battle is brewing over what could be the nation’s first massive data center operating on federal land. And you almost certainly have never heard of it. Come with me to McCracken County, Kentucky, just outside its largest city, Paducah, where the Energy Department is allowing new development at a large brownfield property. First constructed in the 1950s, the Paducah Gaseous Diffusion Plant was once the country’s only uranium enrichment facility, but it closed in 2010. Since then, and after years of cleanup, Paducah city officials and the McCracken County government have sought to revitalize and reindustrialize the site. In July, the Energy Department announced plans for a data center at the site, one with enough power to provide excess electricity to the surrounding community. Brookfield would develop and operate the data center and NextEra Energy would build the power infrastructure — a roughly 2.5 gigawatt natural gas plant — while local and regional electricity companies and co-ops would help provide wholesale and retail electricity. The project would be built alongside new uranium enrichment projects cropping up at the site, as federal officials and companies involved seek to transform the area into what they call an “American energy hub.” Government officials at all levels welcomed the new project. items.title: Contactless continuous guidance of matter in its main states using curved elongated Bessel-like acoustic fields
items.summary_raw: Acoustic manipulation uses sound waves to exert force on matter, enabling contactless movement, trapping, and the structuring of particles in bulk media. It offers a contamination-free approach for handling matter in applications spanning across chemistry, biology, and advanced manufacturing. However, state-of-the-art techniques, including acoustic holograms or phased arrays of transducers (PATs) are limited to transporting individual particles or small clusters one by one, and are not suitable for dispersed matter such as gases or aerosols. Here, we introduce a method for guiding a continuous flow of matter along reconfigurable three-dimensional trajectories using elongated Bessel-like acoustic fields (EBAFs). These fields generate converging radial acoustic forces along a programmable path, forming stable mid-air conduits that continuously transport matter. Compared to existing methods such as near-field acoustic levitation, acoustofluidic separation, particle manipulation with vortex and Airy beams, the proposed method offers enhanced versatility, scalability, and real-time control of transport trajectories in mid-air without requiring physical guiding structures. We developed methods to generate EBAFs with PATs tailored to different particle sizes and material properties, and experimentally demonstrated guidance of solids, liquids, aerosols, and gases along programmable trajectories. This technique enables containerless laboratory operations, precise and…

items.title: Integrating ecology with genetics to explain gene reuse during repeated evolution
items.summary_raw: The role of determinism and chance in the evolutionary history of life is often analyzed through the lens of the repeatability of evolution. Although it is now clear that evolution often repeats itself, we are only beginning to understand why this varies in degree. For example, the probability of gene reuse during repeated bouts of adaptation often declines with time since divergence, but the causes of this pattern remain unclear. Here, we explore two core hypotheses for time-dependent variation in the repeatability of gene reuse during adaptation. Specifically, gene reuse depends on the extent to which lineages have 1) similar genomes such that they have similar genetic architectures, mutations, and mutational effects (i.e., a fairly well-appreciated “shared genetics” hypothesis), and 2) similar ecologies such that they have similar environments and patterns of natural selection (i.e., a mostly unexplored “shared ecology” hypothesis). The latter hypothesis emphasizes ecology’s role in gene reuse and has received little explicit attention. In particular, testing the shared ecology hypothesis requires moving beyond a simple dichotomous characterization of ecology to embracing ecological divergence as a multivariate and continuous phenomenon. Although such tests are only beginning to emerge, they already illustrate how integration of ecological factors can help explain variation in gene reuse. Here, we advocate a framework that integrates the influence of both genetic and…

Susumu Tonegawa (1939–2026): A molecular biologist who transformed immunology and neuroscience
items.summary_raw: Susumu Tonegawa transformed two fields of biology. His discovery of the genetic mechanism generating antibody diversity established the foundations of modern immunology and earned him the 1987 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine. Remarkably, he then began a second scientific career in neuroscience, pioneering genetic approaches to dissect the molecular and circuit mechanisms of learning and memory and, ultimately, the neuronal ensembles that store specific memories. He was also an ambitious institution builder whose leadership shaped neuroscience at Massachusetts Institute of Technology and RIKEN. As former trainees from his immunology and neuroscience labs, we remember a scientist of extraordinary curiosity, intensity, and intellectual courage, who was never afraid to leave familiar territory in pursuit of a fundamental question.

High-resolution measurements of thermal conductivity matrix and search for thermal Hall effect in La 2 CuO 4
items.summary_raw: We investigated the longitudinal thermal conductivity κ xx and thermal Hall conductivity κ xy in La 2 CuO 4 at temperatures T between 2 and 20 K in magnetic fields H up to 10 T. Within the temperature and field intervals studied, we do not resolve any thermal Hall signal with a conservative upper bound of | κ xy / T | < 1 × 10 − 4 Wm − 1 K − 2 . The longitudinal thermal conductivity κ xx / T agrees well with previous reports, in both its magnitude and T dependence. Both κ xx and κ xy were measured using the field-swept protocol. To achieve high resolution, we carefully took into account relaxation effects after each step-increase in H . At low T , we find a weak linear decrease in κ xx / T vs. H , as well as weak hystereses near the metamagnetic transitions of the spins.

items.title: Action features dominate cortical representation during natural vision
items.summary_raw: Cortical resources are allocated into systems specialized for processing ecologically relevant features of the world. These features are typically studied in isolation using controlled experimental stimuli, making it difficult to assess the relative importance of different kinds of features that tend to overlap during natural vision. In the current study, we evaluated the relative contributions of action, agent, and scene features in predicting cortical activity while participants viewed a 1-h nature documentary. We tested four sets of model features: semantic vectors capturing the observed action, agent, and scene features derived from an annotation of the stimulus, as well as low-level visual motion-energy features. We used banded ridge regression to fit vertex-wise encoding models from the combination of all four sets of features. While each set of features predicted neural activity in the expected areas, the action features predicted more widespread activity. A variance partitioning analysis revealed that the action features captured the most unique variance in neural activity across a much larger extent of cortex than the agent or scene features. Our findings suggest that cortical activity during dynamic, natural vision is dominated by features for understanding the actions of others.

items.title: Capillary physics links HIV capsid geometry to nuclear pore translocation
items.summary_raw: The protective capsid encasing the genetic material of HIV can traverse the nuclear pore complex (NPC) intact, despite being far larger than conventional passive cargo. This is attributed to the properties of the capsid surface, which promote partitioning into cohesive assemblies of the disordered proteins that form the NPC’s permeability barrier: phenylalanine-glycine nucleoporins (FG-Nups). The implication, at the mesoscale, is that capsid–NPC interactions are characterized by the interfacial physics of wetting and capillarity. To capture this, we develop a minimal theory that reduces to an interplay between capsid geometry, effective cytoplasmic and nucleoplasmic contact angles, and a ratio of interfacial tensions. By combining analytical calculations, sharp- and diffuse-interface numerics, we make several predictions: A geometry-dependent trade-off between penetration depth and the wetting transition; asymmetric capillary forces that generate torques and lead to metastable “stalled” states that are tilted; a topological classification of the possible mechanisms underlying the largest energetic barrier; and spontaneous symmetry breaking of displaced FG-Nups. These behaviors connect capsid shape and orientation to the topology and symmetry of FG-Nup displacement, and to the molecular compositions on each side of the pore. They are consistent with published cryoelectron tomography orientations, which provide an initial estimate of the cytoplasmic contact angle. Crucially…

items.title: A functional two-pore-domain K + channel from a large DNA virus
items.summary_raw: The evolutionary history of proteins helps to understand their structure/function correlates and suggests on how functional complexity evolved from primitive precursors. In the superfamily of K + channels, functional features of complex eukaryotic inward rectifier (Kir) channels and voltage-dependent (Kv) channels could be understood in terms of an increase in structural complexity of their prokaryotic precursors. K2P channels, which are made from tandem repeats of two pore domains, are not found in prokaryotes and their evolutionary origin is still unknown. In searching for primitive K2P channel precursors, we screened the genomes of nucleocytoplasmic large DNA viruses (NCLDVs) for genes coding for K2P channels. This was motivated by two reasons: NCLDVs are already known for coding primitive Kir type channels, and they play important roles in the evolution of eukaryotes. Here, we report that the NCLDV Pyramimonas orientalis virus codes for K2P-like K + channels. With only 178 amino acids and no cytosolic domains, this Kpov protein is much smaller than any eukaryotic K2P channel, but still functional as K + selective channel in lipid bilayers. Phylogenetic analysis suggests that Kpov is not the product of molecular piracy from the host but may result from fusion of primitive viral K + channel pore domains.

items.title: The revised diploid genome sequence of an individual human: A workflow for near telomere-to-telomere assemblies using only Oxford Nanopore Technologies Simplex-reads
items.summary_raw: The first draft diploid genome assembly (HuRef) of an individual in 2007 was a milestone in genomics. Here, we report HuRef2.0, a revision of HuRef assembled using only Oxford Nanopore Technologies (ONT) Simplex-reads and the hifiasm assembler. Results are close in continuity to the telomere-to-telomere (T2T) assemblies but were assembled from standard DNA samples without using multiple sequencing and mapping technologies, including ultra-long-reads and/or proximity-ligation. Three ONT flowcells (~103× coverage) from fresh blood DNA produced an assembly comprising 26 contigs, with gapless assembly of 23 chromosomes (Chr). Two gaps on ChrY were locally assembled to yield the final T2T-assembly, HuRef2.0, with base accuracy >Q60.34 and 2,393 phase blocks with an NG50 value of 2.36 Mb. Assembly from a single ONT flowcell (~35× coverage) consistently produced an assembly more contiguous than GRCh38.p14, providing a foundation for further optimization and scaling. Assembly quality was assessed by direct chromosome-level alignments to a reference genome, variant calling, and annotation of gene-rich regions at Chr22q11, the extended MHC locus, and at several difficult to assemble regions, including the rRNA gene clusters, the subtelomeric region on Chr4q35, ChrY, and the centromeres. More accurate but shorter Pacific Biosciences HiFi-reads produced less contiguous assemblies than from equivalent coverage of error-corrected ONT reads, indicating the importance of read-length. We…

items.title: Deconfined criticality between an antiferromagnetic insulator and a nodal d -wave superconductor: A quantum Monte Carlo study
items.summary_raw: We present a quantum Monte Carlo study of the transition between the insulating Néel state and the nodal d -wave superconductor on the square lattice at half-filling. We access a regime of frustrated magnetic order without a sign problem using a parton representation of the electron in terms of fermionic spinons and bosonic chargons. Both partons move in a background π -flux (so the electron experiences no net flux) and are coupled to a quantum fluctuating SU(2) lattice gauge field. In contrast to earlier studies directly on the electronic degrees of freedom, we find evidence for a second-order deconfined quantum phase transition at which both the Néel and d -wave superconductivity orders vanish continuously. We compute correlators of the spinon-chargon composite with the same quantum numbers as the electron: we find a gapless Dirac dispersion inside the d -wave superconductor, turning into a gapped dispersion in the antiferromagnet.

items.title: Si-scRNA-seq: Enabling ambient-stable single-cell transcriptomics through spatially confined biosilicification
items.summary_raw: Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) is constrained by rapid RNA degradation during sample storage, necessitating cold-chain logistics. Here we present spatially confined biosilicification (SCB), wherein RNA is encapsulated within a nanoscopic layer of amorphous silicon dioxide, as a highly effective methodology enabling ambient-temperature preservation of single-cell transcriptomes. By judiciously incorporating a silicification inhibitor, SCB achieves spatiotemporal control over both intra- and extracellular silica deposition, preventing excessive crosslinking and cell aggregation while preserving RNA biointegrity and accessibility. scRNA-seq performed with biosilicified cells (Si-scRNA-seq) maintained high transcriptomic fidelity with fresh samples (R 2 = 0.95 after 7 d) extending RNA half-life to 54.8 d at 25 °C, a 685-fold improvement compared to unprotected samples. Furthermore, Si-scRNA-seq confers robust resistance against oxidative and UV degradation. Compatible with mainstream platforms at ~0.1 RMB per sample, Si-scRNA-seq successfully resolves cellular heterogeneity in clinical lung, liver, and ovarian cancer specimens after extended room-temperature storage. Si-scRNA-seq provides a scalable and cold-chain–free solution for single-cell transcriptomics in research and clinical settings.

items.title: Local growth laws determine global shape of molluscan shells
items.summary_raw: Molluscan shells come in various shapes and sizes. Despite this diversity, each species produces a shell with a characteristic shape that is independent of environmental conditions. We seek to understand this robust complexity. We are guided by two principles in the spirit of D’Arcy Thompson. First, the growth is governed by the repeated and continuous application of a fixed growth law, even as the shell evolves in overall shape, without any complex biological machinery to monitor and control the growth. Second, the growth law depends solely on local geometry at the shell’s growing edge. The first principle naturally leads to the mathematical statement that the shape of the shell is generated by the action of a Lie group on a protoconch. The second naturally leads to a particular representation of the Lie group. We use this representation to show that the shapes of nearly all known molluscan shells can be described by essentially three parameters: a scalar (scaling), a vector (orientation), and a curve (edge of the protoconch). We relate these parameters to the phylogenetic tree. In addition to the morphogenetic insight, our results potentially point to a alternative growth-based approach to engineering complex structures.

items.title: Education reduces dementia incidence and mitigates genetic risk
items.summary_raw: There is little causal evidence on factors that can protect individuals against Alzheimer’s Disease and Related Dementias (ADRD) risk. We study the causal effect of education on ADRD, exploiting a regression discontinuity generated by a compulsory schooling reform. ADRD was ascertained based on medical history, hospital records, and death registries, addressing concerns about selective sample attrition. We find that education reduces incidence of ADRD. Using molecular genetic data, we show that the reform weakened the relationship between genetics and ADRD incidence, implying genetic risk of dementia is not immutable and can be modified by social policy.

items.title: Is There Room for Lucid?
items.summary_raw: Jason Fenske loved his Lucid. Or at least, the idea of it. Fenske is the proprietor of the influential Engineering Explained channel on YouTube, which digs into the mechanical minutiae of both combustion and electric vehicles. While he regularly test-drives all sorts of cars, Fenske last year bought himself a Lucid Air, the big, beautiful sedan from the California EV startup. The choice was no surprise. Fenske called the Air “one of the most impressive feats of engineering in the automotive world.” Technologically, it is indeed a car without compromise. Despite delivering 600-plus horsepower and a 0-60 mph time of barely more than 3 seconds, it was also the most efficient car in America, a fact that helped push its driving range above 400 miles per charge. But after a year of Fenske’s Air struggling with seemingly incurable software glitches, the company bought back his car and gave him a long-term loan of the Gravity, its new electric SUV. When that, too, suffered software bugs, he finally moved on to a Ford. The episode encapsulates what has been a trying time for the automaker. Alongside Tesla and Rivian, Lucid looked to be the third successful EV startup to spring out of California. Tesla, once it overcame the trials of “manufacturing hell” to produce the Model 3 and Model Y, seized control of the American EV market and has yet to let go. Rivian, buoyed through the bad years by investments from the likes of Volkswagen and Amazon, appears poised to reach a sustainable…

items.title: Between ecolinguistics and environmental communication: disciplinary boundaries and selective convergence
items.summary_raw: Abstract This article examines the uneven relationship between ecolinguistics and environmental communication through a qualitative thematic analysis of 31 articles published in the journal Environmental Communication between 2016 and 2025. Revisiting earlier concerns about ecolinguistics’ limited interdisciplinary uptake, the article asks whether and how ecolinguistics has entered into sustained dialogue with a neighbouring field likewise concerned with discourse, mediation, power, and environmental crisis. The findings show that the journal has developed a substantial discourse-oriented tradition, with 26 articles using critical discourse analysis or related approaches to examine climate communication, extractivism, environmental justice, species representation, pedagogy, and place. Yet explicit engagement with ecolinguistics remains limited: among five articles mentioning the term, only two treat it as a central framework. I argue that this pattern is best understood as a missed conversation shaped by different disciplinary genealogies and scalar approaches to discourse. Environmental communication has tended to analyze discourse as mediated, institutional, rhetorical, and political communication, while ecolinguistics has offered more linguistically granular tools and more explicit frameworks for ecological evaluation. The article concludes by proposing selective convergence between the two fields, particularly through closer articulation between macro-level analyses of…

items.title: Adapting to extreme heat: how corporate responses enhance customer stability
items.summary_raw: Purpose This paper examines the impact of extreme heat risk on corporate customer stability in the Chinese market. Design/methodology/approach Using a comprehensive dataset from 2012 to 2023, we find that greater exposure to city-level extreme heat risk incentive firms to adopt adaptive adjustments, thereby enhancing customer stability. Findings This effect is mainly achieved through three channels, including optimizing human capital, advancing digital transformation and strengthening supply chain finance. Cross-sectional heterogeneity test reveals that the impact is more pronounced in firms with lower labor intensity, fewer high-skilled employees and limited trade credit access. These findings provide novel evidence on how firms transform climate-related risks into opportunities to strengthen resilience, and offer important implications for corporate adaptation strategies and policy support in the context of global climate change. Originality/value Our research makes several contributions in three major aspects. First and foremost, our findings extend the literature on the economic consequences of extreme heat; furthermore, our research enriches the literature on the determinants of customer stability; last but not least, by examining the mechanism linking extreme heat risks at firm locations to customer stability, our study extends organizational adaptation theory to the context of climate risk and supply chains, enriching the theoretical framework on how climate factors…

items.title: Biodiversity is a key motivation for European urban green space planning and management
items.summary_raw: Abstract Many urban green spaces are ecologically degraded. Yet, when designed and managed using ecologically motivated practices, green spaces can support biodiversity. However, many municipalities have not yet adopted strategies to enhance biodiversity. To better understand the importance assigned to biodiversity in public urban green spaces, we interviewed 574 municipalities across 18 European countries. Using a standardized questionnaire, we examined the underlying motivations, management goals and the measures municipalities used to support the public acceptance of biodiverse green spaces. Most municipalities (85%) reported biodiversity as a key motivation in green space planning and management. Many provided staff training (82%) and took action to increase public acceptance (75%) of biodiversity-promoting management. The reported perceptions of municipalities’ ecological condition were mostly positive, but 19% reported declines in the last decade. Differences between municipalities could be linked to regional and structural factors such as the sealed surface of the municipality, highlighting the need for locally adaptable policies for urban biodiversity.

items.title: Climate warming boosts frequency and intensity of southern Africa’s rainfall extremes
items.summary_raw: Nature Climate Change, Published online: 23 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41558-026-02772-0 Extreme southward swings of the South Indian convergence zone (a major source of rainfall across southern Africa) can trigger devastating floods. Climate-model projections indicate that these swings might occur twice as often in the twenty-first century as in the previous century and produce more intense rainfall, owing to an increased land–sea temperature contrast and poleward intensification of atmospheric circulation.

items.title: Climate Change and Workers’ Health and Safety: An Umbrella Review
items.summary_raw: Background: This umbrella review synthesizes current evidence on the health and safety impacts of climate change among workers. In particular, it aims to identify the main workers’ categories at the highest risk, the main health and safety outcomes, methodological limitations, and future directions reported in the literature, as well as preventive strategies described in recent reviews. Methods: A comprehensive search was conducted in PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science. Systematic and scoping reviews addressing climate-related occupational health and safety outcomes were included. Study selection and data extraction were performed independently by two reviewers. Methodological quality was assessed using the ROBIS tool, and findings were synthesized in accordance with PRISMA and PRIOR guidelines. Results: Most of the available evidence concerns outdoor occupations, particularly agriculture and construction, where exposure to high temperatures is associated with increased risks of injuries and heat strain. Emerging data also highlight links with mental health, renal disease, and chronic conditions. However, the literature remains fragmented, with few meta-analyses and substantial heterogeneity. Preventive strategies have been proposed, but their implementation remains inconsistent. Conclusions: Evidence confirms that climate change has become a determinant of occupational health and safety. Future research should strengthen methodological coherence, adopt longitudinal…

items.title: From Climate Risk Awareness to Climate-Conscious Investment Behavior: the roles of climate disclosure quality, trust, and greenwashing risk
items.summary_raw: Inroduction The present study examines the factors influencing climate-conscious investment behavior among middle-income retail investors in six major metropolitan cities in India using the Stimulus–Organism–Response (S–O–R) framework, Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB), and Signaling theory. Methods Data were collected from 576 middle-income retail investors. Results The findings indicate that Climate Risk Awareness and Perceived Climate Disclosure Quality were positively associated with Trust in Climate Disclosures, which was subsequently associated with Climate-Conscious Investment Attitude, Climate-Conscious Investment Intention, and self-reported Climate-Conscious Investment Behavior, with Perceived Greenwashing Risk acting as a moderator. Discussion The study advances the field of behavioral climate finance by separating Perceived Climate Disclosure Quality as an information-related stimulus from Climate Risk Awareness as an investor-level cognitive antecedent and demonstrates the interplay of trust, attitude, and intention that leads to climate-conscious investment behavior. The results offer valuable guidance for regulators, corporations and financial institutions aiming to foster the adoption of Climate-Conscious Investment Behavior among urban retail investors.

items.title: Interpersonal Communication Environments and Counterarguing Intentions Toward Climate Misinformation: The Role of Personal Climate Discussion Networks, Norms, and Attitudes
items.summary_raw: How everyday social environments shape behavioral responses to environmental information remains a core question in environment–behavior research. This study examines how interpersonal communication environments influence individuals’ intentions to counterargue environmental misinformation. Drawing on Social Capital Theory and the Reasoned Action Approach, we conceptualize personal climate discussion networks as routine social environments that structure subjective norms and attitudes, which in turn motivate behaviorally oriented responses. Using an online survey of 525 U.S. adults exposed to three climate misinformation memes, we estimated structural equation models with 5,000 bootstrap resamples. Communication frequency within personal discussion networks consistently predicted stronger pro-climate subjective norms and attitudes, which robustly predicted counterarguing intentions across stimuli. In contrast, perceived credibility neither directly predicted counterarguing intentions nor mediated the relationships between subjective norms or attitudes and counterarguing intentions. These findings suggest that corrective responses to environmental misinformation are driven less by individual-level cognitive evaluation and more by socially structured interpersonal environments that activate norms and attitudes.

items.title: "From an activist spirit and history": An examination of Midwest professors who teach gender studies in the current political climate
items.source_name: Communication and Theater Association of Minnesota Journal
items.summary_raw: Gender studies is an interdisciplinary field spanning higher education institutions globally. Yet the experiences of scholars within specific regional contexts remain understudied. This study examines the lived personal and pedagogical experiences of gender studies and gender communication scholars in the Midwest. Using a qualitative approach, semi-structured interviews were conducted to explore participants’ experiences, perceived pressures, and responses to the current political and academic climate. Interview questions focused on the challenges scholars face as well as the communicative practices they adopt in response to shifting attitudes toward gender studies. This research seeks to contribute to a deeper understanding of how scholars navigate evolving expectations and policies within higher education and the broader sociopolitical landscape. Using Croucher & Cronn Mills (2025) definition of inductive coding, three themes emerged from analysis of transcripts. These three themes include Pedagogical Commitment to Transformation, Regional Influence on Curriculum, and Varying Levels of Student Engagement.

items.title: The social-psychological determinants of climate action in older adults: a systematic mapping review of studies investigating motivation, beliefs, self-efficacy, values and identity in the context of climate change
items.summary_raw: Older adults have substantial but often under-recognized potential to contribute to climate change mitigation. However, there is currently no systematic review synthesizing the evidence on the social-psychological determinants of climate action in older adulthood. This paper systematically maps existing evidence on the role of motivation, beliefs, self-efficacy, values and identity among older adults in the context of climate change and climate action. Following the PRISMA guidelines for reporting systematic reviews, studies focusing on these psychological determinants in the context of climate change and older adulthood were searched in three major databases (PsycINFO, PubMed and Web of Science). A total of 1,503 articles were returned from the systematic search. Of these, 174 unique studies (185 entries when accounting for articles addressing multiple determinants) published between 2005 and 2024 met criteria for eligibility in the final systematic mapping database (32 for motivation, 87 for beliefs, seven for self-efficacy, 36 for values and 23 for identity). The studies showed a notable geographic distribution, with the majority originating from Europe and the US. The results showed all determinants to be associated with actions aimed at mitigating climate change, with beliefs being the most explored and self-efficacy the least explored construct in the context of climate change and older adults. However, although all studies in the mapping review involved participants…

items.title: Země směřuje k oteplení o 2,8 stupně Celsia proti předindustriálnímu období
