items.title: Water quality for agricultural reuse: integrating risk assessment, governance, and sustainable implementation for resilient food systems
items.summary_raw: Global freshwater scarcity, climate change, and rising food demand have intensified the need for sustainable agricultural water management. Wastewater reuse has emerged as a strategic solution, alleviating water stress, enhancing climate resilience, and supporting circular resource management. However, the long-term sustainability of agricultural water reuse depends critically on water quality that safeguards crop productivity, ecosystem integrity, and public health. This review provides a novel interdisciplinary synthesis by integrating conventional indicators (salinity, nutrients, microbial pathogens) with emerging contaminants (pharmaceuticals, per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances [PFAS], microplastics, antibiotic resistance genes). Unlike previous reviews focused narrowly on treatment or regulation, we combine Quantitative Microbial Risk Assessment (QMRA), chemical and ecological risk evaluation, and AI-assisted multi-criteria decision analysis (AI-MCDA) into a unified framework. We systematically surveyed peer-reviewed literature (Scopus, Web of Science, ScienceDirect, 2010–2025) and international guidelines (WHO, FAO, EU, US EPA, ISO), highlighting both progress and persistent gaps in harmonizing standards. Advances in monitoring technologies IoT sensors, biosensors, remote sensing, and digital twins are critically assessed for their role in real-time surveillance and adaptive governance. Case studies from the Middle East, North Africa, Europe, Australia, the United…

items.title: Strengthening Institutional Governance to Counteract Urban-Driven Carbon Emissions in Central Europe: Insights from Economies in the Black Triangle Industrial Zone
items.summary_raw: Urban expansion and industrial concentration in Central Europe’s historic Black Triangle zone-encompassing Germany, Poland, and the Czech Republic-continue to drive elevated carbon dioxide (CO2) emissions, posing significant challenges to regional climate goals and the downstream ecological stability of the Baltic and North Sea basins. Rapid employment-based urban migration expands built environments, alters land-use patterns, and intensifies energy demand across industrial corridors. This research empirically examines the dynamic long-run impacts of institutional governance, urban migration, and fossil energy consumption on CO2 emissions in three economies across the Black Triangle Industrial zone of Central Europe over the period 1998:Q4 to 2021:Q4. Utilizing the Pooled Mean Group (PMG) estimator within a Panel Autoregressive Distributed Lag (ARDL) framework, the long-run empirical results reveal that: (i) strengthening institutional quality significantly abates CO2 emissions, whereas (ii) both fossil fuel consumption and urban migration exert a statistically significant positive effect on long-run carbon emissions. These insights underscore that robust institutional governance is essential to decoupling urban economic growth from environmental degradation. To achieve UN Agenda 2030 targets and mitigate transboundary environmental impacts-including marine resource degradation and eutrophication in connected Central and Northern European catchments-policy interventions must…

items.title: Political Will and Managing the Impact of Climate Change: Dispatches from Lake Chad
items.summary_raw: This article examines the impact of climate change on Lake Chad from the perspective of the dominant narrative that holds that the lake has shrunk by more than 90% since 1960, with its attendant impact on livelihoods, conflict and forced migration. In the face of this disaster, this study asks whether there are no remedies. This article examines the efforts made by Lake Chad’s riparian states in addressing the problem through plans to resuscitate the Lake from rivers in the region. This venture, known as Inter-Basin Water Transfer, is argued to curtail water shortages in the Sahel Basin and reduce conflict, among other benefits. Yet, the inaction of the riparian states leaves a lot to be desired. This study contends that the lethargy of African governments in addressing issues of climate change is as damaging to human existence as the impact of climate change itself. Addressing Lake Chad’s issues, amid contending climate change narratives, boils down to the political will of the riparian and Lake Chad Basin governments/agencies. This study makes use of secondary data encompassing findings from earth and environmental sciences.

items.title: The Global Significance of Renewable Energy: Contributions to Economic Growth and Environmental Sustainability
items.source_name: International Journal for Research in Applied Science and Engineering Technology
items.summary_raw: Renewable energy has moved from the margins of the global energy system to its leading edge, reshaping how electricity is generated, traded, and valued. This review synthesises recent evidence on the economic and environmental significance of renewable energy at a global scale. On the economic side, it examines investment trends, employment generation, the levelised cost of electricity (LCOE), energy security, and energy access, drawing on the latest data published by the International Renewable Energy Agency (IRENA), the International Energy Agency (IEA), and the International Labour Organization (ILO). On the environmental side, it reviews the contribution of renewables to greenhouse gas (GHG) mitigation, air quality, and the associated trade-offs in land, water, and material use. The review further discusses the policy architecture supporting the global energy transition, including the Paris Agreement and the COP28 tripling pledge, and identifies the principal barriers that continue to constrain deployment: grid integration and intermittency, storage costs, financing gaps in developing economies, and critical-mineral supply chains. The evidence indicates that renewable energy is no longer solely a climate mitigation tool but has become a central pillar of economic competitiveness, energy security, and industrial policy, while significant regional disparities in investment and employment remain a persistent challenge to an equitable global transition.

items.title: The Next Generation of Power-grid Resilience: Long-horizon AI Planning under Deep Climate Uncertainty
items.source_name: Journal of Energy Research and Reviews
items.summary_raw: Power systems face climate-driven extremes, compound hazards, rapid electrification and renewable integration, and infrastructure decisions whose consequences persist for decades. These conditions often cannot be represented by historical patterns or well-defined probability distributions. Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly applied to forecasting, outage prediction, asset management, optimisation and resilience planning, yet most applications remain prediction-centric, whereas long-horizon grid planning takes place under deep uncertainty. This critical narrative review integrates literature from power-systems engineering, machine learning, climate-risk assessment, infrastructure resilience and decision-making under deep uncertainty to examine how AI can move from forecasting toward robust and adaptive planning. We identify a prediction–planning gap created by two mismatches: a temporal mismatch between the horizons over which AI is predictively competent and those over which infrastructure decisions operate, and an uncertainty mismatch between the stationarity assumptions of learned models and the non-stationary, deeply uncertain conditions of future grids. Distribution shift, rare extremes, model disagreement and optimisation fragility limit prediction-centric approaches. AI offers greater long-term value through scenario exploration, surrogate-accelerated simulation, stress testing, vulnerability discovery, robust multi-objective optimisation and adaptive…

items.title: Recomposing Management Education Under Climate Crisis: Towards a Composting Heuristic for Epistemic Change
items.summary_raw: Abstract Management learning and education (MLE) is increasingly critiqued for its reliance on anthropocentric and profit‐maximization paradigms, which fail to adequately address the escalating ecological and climate crises. In this article, we call for an epistemic shift in MLE by introducing the metaphor of composting as a lens for collective reflexive critique. We propose a composting heuristic inspired by the social practices of managing organic matter—landfill, industrial composting and community composting—to help MLE educators critically examine the epistemic foundations, limitations and possibilities that shape their teaching and learning practices. This metaphorical framework highlights an epistemic transition towards a multispecies and regenerative pedagogical paradigm, grounded in relational ontology, care and embodied practice. We argue that engaging with the metaphor of composting—and reflecting critically on one's positioning within the landfill‐industrial‐community composting heuristic—can catalyse a collective endeavour to drive epistemic change in MLE in response to the urgent demands of climate and ecological breakdown.

items.title: Understanding climate risk in finance: from asset pricing to green investment strategies
Negotiating urban energy transitions in Greater Maputo: Street-level politics and infrastructural heterogeneity
items.summary_raw: Research on urban energy transitions in sub-Saharan Africa has focused either on formal governance or on micropolitics in low-income neighborhoods, providing limited insight into how transition policies addressing access, cost recovery, reliability, and greening are contested across heterogeneous urban infrastructural settings. We address this shortcoming by examining the politics of policy implementation in Greater Maputo, Mozambique, through a street-level bureaucracy lens. Drawing on qualitative data, we show how the electricity utility and its staff exercise discretion in an access-first energy transition setting, amid competing accountabilities and uneven material conditions. Across three ideal-typical settings—peri-urban grid-expansion zones, low-income neighborhoods constrained by affordability, and areas demanding premium reliability—we identify policy divergence patterns: illusory implementation, selective enforcement, and informal service differentiation. These patterns help actors to reconcile conflicting demands but also adversely affect service reliability, undermine greening objectives, and increase socio-spatial inequalities across the city. By showing how material conditions mediate implementation choices, we explain how street-level politics reconfigure heterogeneous urban infrastructures.

items.title: From Risk to Resilience: A Narrative Synthesis of Protective Factors and Proposed Mechanisms in Bias-Based Bullying Among Youth (2016–2026)
items.summary_raw: Background/Objectives: Bias-based bullying (BBB) is a public health concern associated with psychological distress, suicidality, school disengagement, and other adverse health and developmental outcomes. This review synthesized empirical evidence on protective factors and examined proposed mechanisms and contextual conditions associated with how they operate. Methods: A theory-informed narrative synthesis was conducted using empirical studies published from 2016 through 2026 identified through APA PsycInfo, APA PsycArticles, ERIC, PubMed, Web of Science, and supplementary searches. Fifty-nine studies met the inclusion criteria and were appraised using the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool. Findings were coded iteratively and interpreted through an integrated ecological and resource-based theoretical framework. Results: Protective factors were identified across individual, interpersonal, and institutional levels. Individual strengths were more often associated with reduced harm than reduced exposure, whereas relational and institutional resources were more frequently associated with protective outcomes. Protective associations varied according to macro climate and policy context, intersecting identities and cumulative targeting, and proximal school and peer activation processes. No single factor was associated with protection for all youth, outcomes, or forms of BBB, and protective associations were often weaker under cumulative exposure. Conclusions: The findings suggest that…

items.title: Teacher Enjoyment and Attitudes Toward Student Struggles in Mathematics: Evidence from Indonesian Elementary Schools
items.summary_raw: Background Teachers’ enjoyment of teaching mathematics is an important affective factor that shapes instructional quality and classroom climate, while productive struggle has become increasingly recognized as a key element of meaningful mathematics learning. However, existing studies have mostly examined these constructs separately or within Western contexts, providing limited evidence from Indonesian elementary schools. This study addresses this gap by examining the relationship between teachers’ enjoyment of teaching mathematics and their attitudes toward students’ productive struggle, while considering their demographic characteristics. It also investigated whether teaching enjoyment predicts supportive attitudes toward productive struggles. Methods A cross-sectional quantitative study was conducted with 209 elementary school teachers from public and private schools in South Sumatra, Indonesia. Data were collected using the Teaching Enjoyment in Mathematics (TEM) and Attitudes Toward Struggle (ATS) scales. Instrument reliability was assessed using Cronbach’s alpha (α). Descriptive statistics, independent-samples t-tests, one-way analysis of variance (ANOVA), Pearson’s correlation, and multiple linear regression analyses were performed using SPSS version 29. Results Teachers’ enjoyment and attitudes toward productive struggle did not differ significantly by gender, school type, or teaching experience. Teaching enjoyment was positively associated with supportive attitudes…

items.title: From evidence to action: a narrative literature review to inform cross-border one health implementation in the Kavango-Zambezi region
items.summary_raw: Introduction Despite growing commitment to One Health, there is limited operational guidance for implementing cross-border approaches in transboundary regions. The Kavango-Zambezi Transfrontier Conservation Area (KAZA-TFCA), spanning the Southern African countries of Angola, Botswana, Namibia, Zambia, and Zimbabwe, faces interconnected challenges at the human-animal-environment interface, including zoonotic disease risks, food insecurity, environmental change, and complex governance. This study synthesises evidence to identify barriers and opportunities for operationalising One Health across KAZA.Theory This narrative review is informed by the One Health framework, which recognises the interdependence of human, animal and environmental health, and draws on a systems perspective to examine cross-border governance, multisectoral collaboration, and community participation in transboundary settings.Method A narrative review, following the PRISMA-ScR guidelines, was conducted of studies published between 2010 and 2024 across nine databases. Thirty-eight studies were thematically synthesised and analysed across six domains: animal health, food security, environmental health, governance, community perceptions, and health and veterinary services.Results Findings show that challenges are driven by cross-border policy fragmentation, disjointed surveillance coordination, unequal resource access, and limited community inclusion in decision-making. Environmental pressures such as climate…

items.title: Putting a time scale on emerging climate change stressors: a Vulnerability Index for Atlantic Ocean marine ecosystem services
items.summary_raw: Marine ecosystem services underpin human wellbeing and support resilient socio-ecological systems, yet existing vulnerability assessments remain fragmented, often focusing on isolated industries and overlooking the whole-system socio-ecological context. To bridge this gap, we develop a comprehensive Vulnerability Index to assess marine ecosystem service vulnerability to emerging climate stressors in the Atlantic. Using high-resolution ocean simulations and moving beyond traditional long-term projections, we employ the Time of Emergence metric to address actionable decision-making timescales (2–3 decades). We found that all Atlantic marine ecosystem services are projected to be exposed to multiple emerging stressors before 2100, though the sequence and the timing of emergence are highly heterogenous. Overall vulnerability is highest in tropical West Africa due to the early emergence of hypoxia and sea level rise extremes compound by low adaptive capacity. Additional hotspots are found in subpolar and polar regions driven by rapid sea ice retreat and the sensitivities of region-specific habitats alongside a high dependence on marine ecosystems. Coupled with socio-ecological data, we determined which services (provisioning, regulatory and cultural) are most sensitive to potential impacts in each EEZ. We anticipate this index to be a starting point to develop targeted vulnerability indices for specific ecosystem services and regions. Mitigative and adaptive efforts must be…

items.title: Optimizing building envelope and window frame design for high-performance mixed-mode office buildings
items.summary_raw: In tropical climates, mixed-mode ventilation (MMV) is essential for optimizing thermal and energy performance in office buildings. This study investigates the impacts of wind-driven natural ventilation (NV) strategies and window frame design on the thermal and energy performance of MMV office buildings. A database of office buildings in São Paulo was used to develop a representative model to simulate various NV strategies and window frame configurations. artificial neural networks were employed to generate metamodels for annual cooling loads and cooling-degree hours, identifying optimal theoretical scenarios. Findings demonstrate that a holistic design integrating window-to-wall ratio (WWR), window frame design, and solar orientation is critical. In São Paulo's context, cross-ventilation on adjacent facades outperformed single-sided ventilation, reducing cooling loads by up to 25% and increasing air changes per hour (ACH) fourfold. The results emphasize treating WWR and orientation as integrated variables, notably, increasing WWR can serve as a deliberate cooling strategy if the resulting boost in NV potential offsets the higher thermal loads of larger glazed areas. This research underscores the significance of optimized envelope and window design in achieving energy-efficient MMV office buildings

items.title: Cost-effectiveness analysis of climate mitigation measures to achieve greenhouse gas reduction targets in the water sector: a case study of South Korea
items.summary_raw: ABSTRACT The water sector remains underrepresented in climate policy despite its role in greenhouse gas mitigation. This study develops a facility-level cost-effectiveness analysis framework for South Korea's water sector by harmonizing system boundaries, capital expenditure/operation and maintenance expenditure, energy savings, grid emission factors, and technology lifetimes. By using a measure-level database, we evaluate five implementation scenarios. Results show substantial heterogeneity in cost-effectiveness. Scenario D provides the least-cost economic benchmark, achieving high reductions at negative net cost, whereas Scenario E offers a renewables-inclusive and policy-feasible roadmap, achieving a 71% reduction at 10,762 KRW/tCO2eq with a total program cost of 32.7 billion KRW. The sensitivity analysis indicates that cost-to-effectiveness ratio is most responsive to installation cost, technology lifetime, and energy-saving benefits. The proposed framework supports transparent, budget-feasible mitigation portfolio design and can be adapted to other countries by replacing country-specific emission factors, costs, facility inventories, and policy thresholds.

items.title: Beyond climate migration: the right to remain and the right to development as complementary frameworks for climate mobility governance in Africa
items.summary_raw: Introduction Legal and policy responses to climate mobility remain overwhelmingly oriented toward displacement, relocation and cross-border protection, overlooking the right of people to remain in their homes under conditions of dignity and security. In Africa, where climate mobility is substantially governance-determined, this migration-centered orientation leaves both displaced and immobile populations inadequately protected, and overlooks the potential of the right to development to govern the terms of relocation where movement proves unavoidable. Methods The article employs a qualitative doctrinal legal methodology, undertaking close textual analysis of binding and non-binding international, continental and sub-regional instruments, read alongside African Commission and African Court jurisprudence, and triangulated against empirical and policy evidence from the IPCC, IOM, AfDB, UNEP, IDMC and the World Bank. Results The analysis shows that the right to remain and the right to development, though rooted in distinct provisions of the African Charter on Human and Peoples’ Rights (Articles 20, 22 and 24) and the Kampala Convention, function as complementary rather than competing entitlements. The right to remain requires states to invest in anticipatory adaptation, secure land tenure and support community participation, so that migration becomes a matter of genuine choice; the right to development, read through the African Commission and Court’s jurisprudence in Endorois and…

items.summary_raw: This is Heatmap Daily, a weekday digest written by our executive editor. Subscribe here. My colleague Emily Pontecorvo has a fascinating story today about Net Power, an energy and power development company whose technology once seemed key to decarbonizing the country’s electricity grid. When Net Power went public in 2023, it was working on a natural gas-burning power plant that would generate little to no emissions in part by using carbon capture and storage. Its invention seemed to have big implications, and not just for the company’s bottom line: Back then, the Environmental Protection Agency was drafting climate rules that would have required new natural gas plants built in the 2030s to capture their carbon dioxide emissions. Net Power’s technology seemed like one of the best available ways to meet that standard. Cut to 2026, and the world looks different. Thanks to the artificial intelligence boom, electricity demand is surging. But Net Power hasn’t successfully commercialized its proprietary power plant technology. Even if it had, few companies are willing to pay the high premium required by Net Power’s technology, especially when cheaper options are available. And the government certainly isn’t going to require it. Emily’s story reveals what happened next . items.title: Europe’s hottest summer ever was also its deadliest — by far
items.summary_raw: Climate scientists have already established that Europe’s sweltering summer was the hottest on record. Now they are saying it was likely the deadliest as well, with their models showing that the extreme heat led to more than 50,000 excess deaths in cities alone. The continent has endured five scorching heat waves since May, with record-shattering temperatures in several countries . On the whole, it was about 5.2 degrees Fahrenheit (2.9 degrees Celsius) above the 1991 to 2020 average. Some days exceeded the norm by nearly 22 degrees F, or 12 degrees C. Researchers modeled the impact of those extremes across 854 urban areas, representing roughly 40 percent of the population, and the 2026 data, released today, showed that this summer was by far the deadliest on record. “We’re seeing significantly higher modeled deaths,” said Clair Barnes, an extreme weather and climate change researcher at Imperial College London’s Centre for Environmental Policy. The next closest years were 2022 and 2003, with 29,000 and 28,000 excess deaths, respectively. Climate change is making extreme heat more likely, frequent, and persistent. As the mercury climbs, conditions become increasingly dangerous, Barnes said, with even fractions of a degree dramatically raising health risks. She and her colleagues attributed some two-thirds of the 50,000 deaths in their study, which the journal Nature Health will publish next week, to human-caused warming. “Any one of those heat waves would have been deadly…

items.title: Net Power Surrendered Its Clean Dreams to Data Center Demand
items.summary_raw: All kinds of companies have refashioned themselves to exploit the AI boom. A bitcoin miner became a data center developer , a shoemaker is building GPUs , and an electric vehicle company is integrating its powertrains into server racks . Now, a company that once aspired to build one of the lowest-emitting power plants has pivoted to building one of the dirtiest in order to meet data centers’ requirement for speed to power above all. Net Power was founded to pioneer a new form of natural gas power plant with zero emissions, but it has given up on that technology and recently acquired 10 natural gas reciprocating engines that it plans to co-locate with a data center on the site intended for its first commercial plant. “We believe the clean piece is important,” Net Power CEO Danny Rice said during an August earnings call when he announced the company’s pivot to building unabated natural gas plants. “But just as it’s always been, it will only come at scale once society’s basic energy pillars of reliable, affordable power are fully in place. Power demand is outstripping supply today.” Net Power’s pivot is a sign not only that the AI boom has eroded market appetite for clean power, but that U.S. policies supporting carbon capture — primarily the 45Q tax credit that President Trump’s One Big Beautiful Bill Act recently expanded — are still not enough to support the technology’s deployment in the power sector. “The long history of doing CCS in the United States is there isn’t enough…

items.title: m 7 G modification in mRNA cooperates with QKI to promote homologous recombination repair
items.summary_raw: DNA double strand breaks (DSBs) are repaired through distinct pathways, with homologous recombination (HR) favored when DNA ends undergo extensive resection. Although cytoplasmic N7-methylguanosine (m7G)-modified RNA increases after UV-induced single-strand breaks, its role in DSB repair (including HR) remains unclear. Here, we show that m7G-modified RNA accumulates at DSB sites, where it recruits the m7G reader protein Quaking (QKI)5, to selectively promote HR. Mechanistically, QKI5 directly interacts with MRE11 and enhances its DNA binding affinity, thereby facilitating DNA end resection. Depletion of QKI5 impairs recruitment of the MRE11–RAD50–NBS1 complex to DSBs and reduces HR repair efficiency. Moreover, elevated QKI5 expression is associated with resistance to radiotherapy in both mouse models and clinical cohorts. Together, these findings identify the m7G RNA–QKI5–MRE11 axis as a regulator of HR pathway choice and suggest QKI5 as a promising therapeutic target in cancer treatment.

items.title: System-level reorganization of gene networks underlies the nurse-to-forager transition in honeybees
items.summary_raw: Division of labor in social insects is enabled by coordinated changes in physiology, neural signaling, and gene regulation, yet it remains unclear to what extent behavioral maturation reflects incremental changes in individual genes and/or a reorganization of transcriptomic regulation at the system level. Here, we analyze the nurse-to-forager transition in worker honeybees ( Apis mellifera ) from a network perspective, treating the transcriptome as a gene–gene correlation system whose global organization reflects collective regulatory states. Using fat body gene expression data across five developmental time points that span an interval of behavioral transition, we construct signed gene–gene correlation networks and quantify their macro- and mesostate properties. We then descend to the level of the gene and construct microstate gene lists of interacting genes. Behavioral maturation of worker honeybees is accompanied by coordinated, nonmonotonic changes in global network structure rather than simple global shifts in interaction strength across the network. Early stages exhibit broadly positive, globally synchronized correlations, whereas later stages show increased modular segregation and the emergence of antagonistic gene–gene relationships. Despite this differentiation, networks remain fully connected with high global efficiency, consistent with a flexible small-world–like organization. Positive correlations primarily support global integration, while negative correlations…

items.title: Blinks are strategically coupled with head movements in unconstrained natural gaze behavior
items.summary_raw: Blinks are a ubiquitous yet largely unnoticed aspect of human vision, despite causing frequent interruptions of visual input that can amount to up to 10% of waking time. By leveraging a large dataset of unconstrained gaze behavior during two natural tasks, we found a behavioral strategy to limit the impact of blinks: blinks were strategically coupled with head movements, which minimizes information loss due to unreliable visual input during head movements. Specifically, blink probability increased with higher head velocities and showed strong temporal modulation relative to head movement onset: Blink probability was reduced before head movement initiation and then peaked during the head movement. The strength of this coupling was tailored to the individual needs of participants, with participants with higher baseline blink rates showing stronger synchronization. This indicates that blinks are a part of an individually coordinated strategy when orchestrating eye and head movements during unconstrained natural behavior.

items.title: The survival paradox of close-in planets orbiting red-clump giants
items.summary_raw: Close-in planets orbiting core-helium-burning red-clump giants directly challenge tidal-engulfment theory, which predicts that planets within about 1 au of Sun-like stars should be engulfed during red-giant-branch (RGB) expansion. The existence of such survivors would imply missing physical processes in the late stages of stellar and planetary evolution. Yet only one such “forbidden” planet had been identified to date. Here we report three systems—24 Boo b, HD 12648 b, and TYC 4282-605-1 b—whose host stars are confirmed red-clump giants through asteroseismology, showing that each has already undergone dramatic expansion and contraction following helium ignition. Their planets now reside at orbital separations smaller than the maximum stellar radii attained during the RGB phase, implying that they should not have survived. Among them, 24 Boo b orbits at only 0.183 au with a 30-d period, making it the closest planet known around a red-clump giant. These findings demonstrate that this paradox is not an isolated anomaly but signals the emergence of a class of evolved planetary systems. Their survival defies current models of stellar–planetary coevolution and points to unexplored physics shaping planetary architectures around post-RGB stars.

items.title: Mechanistic insight into conflicting valence fluctuation of Cu(I) photocorrosion pathways: The role of charge behaviors
items.summary_raw: Photocorrosion remains a major challenge that hinders the development of photoelectrochemical (PEC) solar fuel production. Although Cu 2 O is a promising photocathode material due to its suitable band structure and visible light absorption, both oxidative and reductive photocorrosion pathways have been reported, with no consensus established in the research community in the PEC system. In this work, we fabricate three Cu 2 O photocathodes with distinct charge transport properties to investigate the correlation between charge accumulation and photocorrosion behavior. Both oxidative and reductive photocorrosion were observed depending on the type and location of charge accumulation. Notably, we propose a refined oxidative photocorrosion mechanism in which photogenerated holes induce surface Cu 2 O dissolution to Cu 2+ , followed by coordination with adsorbed *OH to form Cu(OH) 2 /CuO under illumination, which is contrary to the widely assumed direct oxidation from Cu 2 O to CuO. This work not only provides a unified understanding of the dual photocorrosion pathways in Cu 2 O, but also offers a generalizable framework for understanding photo-induced degradation in metal oxide photocathodes and for guiding the design of more robust PEC systems through charge transport engineering.

Reduction of aflatoxin contamination in maize kernels mediated by host-induced gene silencing
items.summary_raw: Aflatoxins produced by some species of Aspergillus pose a significant threat to global food safety, because they contaminate a variety of crops including maize. In this study, we used host-induced gene silencing (HIGS) to reduce aflatoxin accumulation in maize upon infection with Aspergillus flavus and Aspergillus parasiticus . Two RNAi constructs were designed and introduced into maize, one targeting two essential fungal genes involved in ergosterol biosynthesis ( CYP51A and CYP51B ) and the other targeting three aflatoxin biosynthesis genes ( AflC , AflD , and AflR ). The presence of RNAi transgenes was confirmed in 17 and 14 independent lines possessing the CYP51A/CYP51B RNAi construct and the AflC/AflD/AflR RNAi construct, respectively. Most transgenic lines had single-locus integrations and one or two copies of the transgene. Transgene expression varied considerably among the lines. Small RNA sequencing confirmed the production of siRNAs from the HIGS trigger sequences. Levels of CYP51A , AflC , AflD, and AflR transcripts in Aspergillus spp. were successfully decreased upon infection of transgenic maize. However, significant reduction in the level of CYP51B transcripts was not achieved and the CYP51A/CYP51B RNAi transgene had no discernible effect on fungal growth in infected maize. In contrast, we observed significant reductions in aflatoxin accumulation in four AflC/AflD/AflR RNAi transgenic lines infected with A. flavus and in two transgenic lines infected with A…

items.title: c-FLIP loss links arrest of gene expression to TNFα-dependent antiviral guard immunity
items.summary_raw: Cells sense infection through dedicated receptors, yet these surveillance pathways are often subverted by pathogen-encoded virulence factors. Guard immunity provides complementary defense by rapidly killing infected cells in response to infection induced stress. However, the symptoms of infection frequently resemble noninfectious stress, raising the question of how they are distinguished. Using quantitative transcriptomics, proteomics, and global translation measurements during viral infections in vitro and in vivo, we show that infection globally suppresses host gene expression and prevents direct antiviral responses. However, the resulting proteostatic stress does not activate guard immunity unless tumor necrosis factor-α (TNFα) is present. We identify the anti-apoptotic protein c-FLIP as a guard for gene expression integrity: its loss sensitizes cells to TNFα, triggering cell death and limiting viral spread. Modeling demonstrates that TNFα and c-FLIP loss function as a biological AND-gate, providing specificity and speed. These findings show how cells integrate internal stress signals with external inflammatory cues to improve the fidelity of death decisions, and how this circuitry may misfire during noninfectious inflammation.

items.title: HAP40 functions as a proteostasis regulator by controlling huntingtin interactions and its release into the extracellular space
items.summary_raw: Huntingtin-associated protein 40 (HAP40) forms a stable protein complex with huntingtin (HTT). Its cellular function and how HAP40 loss influences mutant HTT (mHTT) abundance and pathobiology are currently unclear. Here, using diverse cellular models and omics methods, we demonstrate that HAP40 is an obligate interaction partner of HTT and through its binding controls HTT interactions and the abundance of HTT-associated proteins, indicating that it functions as a HTT interaction regulatory unit. Also, loss of HAP40 in mHTT-expressing striatal cells impairs autophagic protein degradation and triggers transcriptional activation of the CLEAR network, demonstrating that it functions as a proteostasis regulator that acts on quality control pathways. Finally, mHTT-expressing cells lacking HAP40 showed increased secretion of a ~205 kDa mHTT fragment through an endoplasmic reticulum (ER)/Golgi-associated route, indicating that striatal cells reduce intracellular mHTT-induced proteotoxicity through activation of secretory pathways. Together, these results establish HAP40 as a critical proteostasis regulator that through controlling HTT interactions maintains cellular homeostasis.

items.title: Virus transmission required for maintenance and host adaptation mirrors neurophysiological differences in rabies-derived peptides
items.summary_raw: Pathogen adaptations to new hosts are central to the disease ecology of cross-species transmission and host switching of viruses. The rabies virus is a model for adaptations to different hosts as it induces behavioral changes that facilitate transmission, while being maintained in distinct species-specific cycles of infection. Here, we demonstrate that the rabies virus requires distinct transmission dynamics in two hosts with different ecologies to establish maintenance, using agent-based modeling, analyses of virus glycoprotein-mediated manipulation of neuroreceptor function, and phylogenetic analysis. Epidemiological models suggest that rabies virus variants adapted to arctic foxes, which sustain rabies virus at very low host densities, require a higher probability of transmission than viruses adapted to raccoons. Using in vitro electrophysiology, we demonstrate that the rabies glycoprotein-derived peptides from arctic fox rabies variants are more potent antagonists of alpha7 nicotinic acetylcholine receptors. These findings suggest a possible functional basis for the behavioral modifications that drive enzootic rabies transmission in the context of host ecology. In addition, a large proportion of residues that may drive rabies virus adaptation to raccoons and arctic foxes are found within this neurotoxin-like region. Furthermore, a residue in the neurotoxin-like region of the mature rabies virus glycoprotein (residue 183) has been associated with pathogenicity, host…

items.title: Neuropharmacology of language: ERP evidence for catecholaminergic modulation of syntactic processing
items.summary_raw: A few studies have shown that brain catecholamines are implicated in language comprehension. However, the specific cognitive processes they modulate remain underexplored. We hypothesized that catecholamines enhance the unification of syntactic roles and word meanings into coherent multiword structures. This study combined electroencephalography and psychopharmacology to examine the effects of a catecholaminergic stimulant (methylphenidate) on processing sentences containing local syntactic ambiguities. Methylphenidate amplified the P600 event-related potential effect, which has been linked to the recruitment of cognitive resources for processing sentences with increased syntactic load. The drug’s impact on semantic processing was subtler, showing a suggestive attenuation of the N400 effect to ambiguous sentences. Furthermore, the increase in the P600 effect under methylphenidate was most pronounced in participants with lower working memory capacity. This study provides evidence for linking catecholamine activity to syntactic unification in healthy individuals. Elevated catecholamine levels appear to increase the cognitive effort invested in syntactic unification, and to support the dynamic prioritization of syntactic information when contextual demands require it.

items.title: Superlubricity by glycerosome boundary layers
items.summary_raw: The search for high-performance lubricants is of broad relevance to biomedical applications, including artificial joints, regenerative scaffolds, and osteoarthritis therapies. Here we introduce glycerosomes—phosphatidylcholine (PC)-based vesicles containing glycerol—as a promising boundary lubricant. Using a surface force balance, we show that glycerosomes achieve a friction coefficient as low as 10 − 5 under a high compression pressure of 15.6 MPa, representing a 20-fold reduction compared to conventional PC liposomes. This level of lubrication surpasses any previously reported boundary lubricant system at such pressures in aqueous media. Mechanistically, glycerosomes exhibit substantially lower adhesion energy than PC liposomes, and theoretical simulations reveal enhanced vesicle stability and flexibility. Our findings establish glycerosomes as a superior hydration lubrication platform, with promising implications for both biomedical implants and industrial applications requiring robust lubricity.

items.title: Google Bets Big on Virtual Power Plants With 1 Gigawatt Voltus Deal
items.summary_raw: North America has about 37.5 gigawatts of total virtual power plant capacity, according to energy consultancy Wood Mackenzie’s latest estimate, published last year. That capacity is spread across roughly 2,000 VPPs, which aggregate distributed energy resources like batteries, smart thermostats, and heat pumps to cut, shift, or supply electricity when the grid is under strain — effectively turning them into a single, coordinated power plant. On Thursday, Google and VPP operator Voltus announced plans to add another 1 gigawatt of clean capacity over the next three or four years — or nearly 3% of North America’s existing total. Under Voltus’ “ bring your own capacity ” model, Google will fund the VPP to help meet its booming data center power needs, while Voltus will enroll businesses and households across the PJM Interconnection, the notoriously overstrained grid region spanning parts of the Midwest and Mid-Atlantic, compensating them for their participation either directly or through electricity bill credits. The announcement expands on a three-year, 100-megawatt deal the two companies signed in June, extending their commitment through 2040. Voltus CEO Dana Guernsey told me that the smaller deal gave the companies a starting point for a much more ambitious partnership. “It’s a lot easier to explain to people how you’re going to 10x if you’ve already 1x, and so we had to start somewhere,” she said. “We always had our eyes set on bigger things.” Earlier this month, Voltus…

The hidden history of how Big Oil invented the American Dream
items.summary_raw: What does going on a date have to do with fossil fuels? Everything, according to the petroleum industry. One advertisement from the pipeline company Energy Transfer follows two people getting ready for a date, the man primping with hair gel, the woman applying lipstick, before meeting at a bar. “That connection was brought to you by petroleum products,” the narrator says. “But what if we lived in a world without oil and natural gas?” The story rewinds to the beginning, except this time, the woman looks bewildered as her phone with the dating app evaporates in her hands. She gets lipstick all over her cheek when the car she’s riding in hits the pavement without its tires. As his hair gel disappears, the man looks into the mirror, baffled. When they sit down across from each other, makeup, hair dye, and glasses fade away. In the game playing on a TV in the bar, a football disintegrates a second before the kicker swings his leg at empty air. The commercial , which has racked up 7.4 million views since it appeared four years ago, taps into the fact that fossil fuels have become embedded in American life (what’s more American than football?). Oil and gas not only influence how people get around town, but also where they live, how they dress, and how they cook food in their kitchens. This all feels so ordinary that most people don’t notice how pervasive petroleum is, powering our lives while hiding in plain sight. Though it might seem inevitable that we live this way, a Grist…

items.title: Fossil fuels are hiding all over your house. We built a model home to show how.
items.summary_raw: Freeing yourself from oil is a downright impossible task in modern America. You could put solar panels on your roof, bring tote bags to the grocery store, and drive an electric vehicle, but try as you might, your home would still be brimming with products derived from fossil fuels. Roughly 9 out of every 10 things in a typical home have some kind of chemical basis in petroleum, according to John Warner, an inventor who co-founded the field of “ green chemistry .” It’s easy to miss all these innocent-looking items, because they’re hiding in plain sight. After World War II, a budding industry fueled by petroleum rapidly expanded — and the products hardly resembled crude oil. They were Tupperware containers, nylon stockings, and Tide laundry detergent. Chemical companies called these synthetic items “miracle” products that would revolutionize home living, promising comfort and convenience. For oil companies, the home was a new frontier. In an alphabet-themed advertising campaign from Shell in 1956, “H” was for Home; the company pointed out that oil research helped with everything from quick-drying paints and no-polish floor tiles to weather-defying asphalt-shingled roofs. items.title: Soaring oil prices underscore the need to help poor countries adopt renewables
items.summary_raw: War-induced spikes in oil prices and the arrival of artificial intelligence are widening the economic gap between rich and poor countries, according to the International Monetary Fund’s October report on the world economy . Poorer countries that import most of their fossil fuels have suffered the worst consequences of the United States’ and Israel’s war on Iran, while wealthier countries have better withstood war-related shocks thanks to AI-related economic growth and diversified energy systems, the report said. Renewable and clean energy could help poorer countries strengthen their economies against future economic turbulence, but a well-planned energy transition requires resources these countries don’t have. Instead, families and companies in developing countries are pursuing their own ad hoc energy transitions with cheap electric motorbikes and rooftop solar panels. Demand for an energy transition in poor economies is here, experts say, but no one is providing the planning and money to make it orderly or equitable. “Getting off oil is the only solution to this long-standing, but currently very acute, economic vulnerability,” said Rebecca Ray, an economist studying global sustainable development at Boston University. “The question is, who’s going to pay for it?” Oil and gas prices, which have soared as wars in the Middle East and Ukraine have destroyed refineries and closed shipping routes, have made all kinds of products more expensive, including fertilizer and goods that…

items.title: California just showed how home batteries will radically remake the grid
items.summary_raw: Until recently, you’ve had no choice but to be a passive participant in the electrical grid, paying exorbitantly for the juice that flows into your home. But you’re about to play a much more active role — if you’re not already — and get paid to send power from your home battery or electric vehicle to the energy system. Even if you’re a renter, you may be able to buy solar panels that plug into a wall outlet, turning your balcony into your own tiny power plant . Earlier this month, a punishing California heat wave showed just how this more flexible grid can help absorb spikes in demand. According to the energy-focused nonprofit Common Charge, as the mercury climbed on October 6 , home batteries from Tesla and Sunrun provided enough to power every home in San Francisco and San Jose , whose combined population is about 1.8 million, during peak hours. This sort of adaptability doesn’t just help stabilize the grid, and it doesn’t just compensate the people who supply power — it saves all ratepayers money in the long run . “It also helps the neighbor who doesn’t have solar and batteries,” said Mary Rafferty, executive director of Common Charge. That’s because drawing on energy that’s stored locally is cheaper than building new gas plants or importing electricity from other states when demand outstrips local supply. items.title: Heatwave-induced capacity bottlenecks in European electricity grids
items.summary_raw: Abstract Heatwaves are becoming more frequent, intense and prolonged as the climate warms, placing stress on the electricity infrastructure underpinning modern societies. Yet how rising temperatures erode grid capacity remains under-quantified. Existing power-flow models either oversimplify thermal effects or become computationally intractable when resolving them in detail. Here we introduce a unified, computationally efficient framework that jointly captures temperature-dependent demand, generator derating and spatially resolved transmission-line thermal limits within an alternating-current optimal power-flow formulation. Applying it to the Western European system with open-access grid, high-resolution weather reanalysis and demand data, we simulate hundreds of projected heatwave scenarios for 2026–2030. Across these represented grid configurations, the analysis reveals substantial national disparities: the Spanish grid exhibits temperature-induced bottlenecks and load shedding, whereas the German grid remains comparatively resilient. Heatwave-aware power-flow analysis thus uncovers structural bottlenecks and should be integrated into grid planning and adaptation as heatwaves intensify under climate change.

items.title: Investigation of the Relationship Between Social-Emotional Learning Skills and Xenophobic Attitudes Among Athletes
items.summary_raw: This study examined the relationship between athletes’ social-emotional learning skills and xenophobic attitudes. Using a correlational design, the study included 188 licensed athletes aged 18 years and older residing in Istanbul, recruited through convenience sampling. The participants comprised 124 men and 64 women. Data were collected in November 2024 through face-to-face and online administration of a Personal Information Form, the Xenophobia Scale, and the Social Emotional Learning Scale–Young Adult Form. Analyses included descriptive statistics, independent-samples t tests, one-way analysis of variance, and Pearson correlations. Social-emotional learning scores did not differ significantly by gender or age group. Total social-emotional learning scores were higher among individual-sport athletes than team-sport athletes and among amateur athletes than professional and elite athletes. Total social-emotional learning scores showed a weak, statistically significant negative correlation with group-centrism. Responsible decision-making and relationship skills were also negatively associated with group-centrism. Tolerance toward other groups was not significantly associated with total social-emotional learning scores or any of its subscale scores. The findings suggest that certain components of social-emotional learning are associated with lower group-centrism. The weak associations and cross-sectional design limit causal interpretations.

Citizenship at Sea: A Comparative Perspective on Blue Justice in the Andaman Sea and the Mediterranean in the Context of Climate Change
items.summary_raw: Discourses of the ocean in the sociological and socio-legal world have, until recently, been approached from majoritarian, terrestrial, profane and nation-centric perspectives. These perspectives are embedded in legal and regulatory regimes to the detriment of Indigenous and marginalized maritime communities. Drawing on the blue turn in sociology and socio-legal scholarship, this Article, in comparing the experiences of the Moken people of the Andaman Sea with those of migrants, fishers, and island communities in the Mediterranean, exposes the violence of such narratives. Through a comparative analysis of maritime borders, marine protected areas, tourism, and fisheries regulation, the Article explores how governance regimes can restrict mobility, undermine customary practices, and produce forms of exclusion without necessarily requiring physical displacement. It argues that climate adaptation and marine conservation cannot be assessed solely through ecological or security objectives, but must also account for their distributional and socio-cultural consequences. By proposing an instrumentalizing of the interconnected theses of the sociological blue turn, and the deterrestrification of the sea, a conception of blue justice that recognizes the sea as a socially inhabited and ecologically interconnected space, is advanced. And a call is put out for maritime governance that incorporates Indigenous and customary practices, and the rights of communities whose relationships with…

items.title: The Impact of Greenfield Investment in Renewables on Energy Poverty
items.summary_raw: In the context of the global energy transition and the continuous advancement of sustainable development goals, how Renewable Energy Greenfield Investments can improve energy accessibility, reduce energy use costs and alleviate energy poverty has become an important issue in energy economics research.This study investigates the impact of Renewable Energy Greenfield Investments on energy poverty using panel data from 153 countries from 2003 to 2023.This study employs a two-way fixed effects model and further conducts endogeneity tests and a series of robustness checks. The results provide the following observations. First, Renewable Energy Greenfield Investments significantly reduces energy poverty. Second, its mitigating effect varies across countries and regions. Third, the effect shows greater strength in non-high-income countries. Moreover, the mechanism analysis based on the interaction between Renewable Energy Greenfield Investments and electricity consumption indicates that Renewable Energy Greenfield Investments plays a stronger role in alleviating energy poverty in countries with lower electricity consumption levels.Hence, this research provides stronger support for the role of Renewable Energy Greenfield Investments in mitigating energy poverty. This paper further delves into the policy implications arising from the findings.

items.title: Public perception and acceptance of biotechnology in agriculture: insights from Poland
items.summary_raw: Agricultural biotechnology encompasses a range of technologies, including genetically modified organisms (GMOs), which have been developed and applied in agriculture for several decades, as well as the more recently developed new genomic techniques (NGTs), which have attracted increasing attention in the context of challenges related to sustainable agriculture and food security. However, its successful implementation depends not only on technological progress but also on public acceptance. This study presents a structured literature review synthesizing the existing evidence on public acceptance of agricultural biotechnology in Poland. Relevant studies were identified through a structured search of the Scopus and Web of Science databases using predefined search terms related to public acceptance, perceptions, attitudes, GMOs, NGTs, and Poland. The reviewed literature was analyzed to identify patterns in public awareness, perceptions, attitudes, and the main determinants influencing technology acceptance. The review shows that research conducted in Poland has focused predominantly on GMOs, while empirical evidence on public perceptions of NGTs remains scarce. Public acceptance is strongly influenced by the application context, perceived risks and benefits, trust in science and institutions, and the level of public awareness. Biotechnology applications associated with health and environmental benefits generally receive greater support than those related to food production. The…

items.title: Do Climate Risks Precede Climate Communication? Global Evidence From Central Banks
items.summary_raw: ABSTRACT Climate change increasingly intersects with central bank mandates through macroeconomic volatility, financial stability, and systemic risk. This study examines whether physical climate vulnerability, institutional readiness, and domestic climate‐policy intensity shape climate‐related central bank communication using a global panel of central bank speeches from 1996 to 2024. The results show that greater climate vulnerability and stronger climate‐policy intensity are associated with higher subsequent climate discourse, while institutional readiness is also positively related to communication in several specifications. The effect of vulnerability is strongest among central banks that already communicate more intensively about climate issues. Predictive tests further indicate temporal ordering from vulnerability to climate discourse, with weaker evidence that communication precedes subsequent policy development. A supplementary Paris Agreement analysis shows that climate communication increased after 2016 across vulnerability groups, but more rapidly among low‐ and medium‐vulnerability countries. The findings suggest that central bank climate communication responds to climate‐related exposure, while its intensity also depends on institutional readiness and the broader policy environment.

items.title: Does school climate matter? The impact of mastery, performance and student voice climate on promoting school effectiveness
items.summary_raw: Abstract The study reported in this paper investigates the impact of four aspects of school climate (i.e. mastery learning climate, performance learning climate, student voice support and children's voice practices) on student learning outcomes. Drawing on panel data of the Children's School Lives national longitudinal study of Irish primary schooling, this paper investigates whether any of these aspects of school climate predict changes in schools' effectiveness status. Data from around 1500 students participating at each time point were analysed. School effectiveness was measured in terms of schools' contribution to student academic achievement in reading and mathematics, after controlling for student background characteristics. School climate constructs were measured using teacher reports, with construct validity and measurement invariance across time established. Multilevel modelling techniques were used to classify schools, at first, based on their effectiveness status at each time point, and subsequently, based on changes in their effectiveness status across time points (i.e. improvement, stability or decline). Discriminant function analyses investigate whether changes in school climate constructs predict changes in schools' effectiveness status. Mastery learning climate, student voice support and children's voice practices were found to predict changes in schools' effectiveness status across time periods and subjects. However, performance learning climate was found to…

items.title: Electoral Propaganda and Public Opinion Formation in Nigeria's Fourth Republic: A Conceptual Analysis
items.source_name: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
items.summary_raw: Electoral propaganda has become a structural feature of democratic competition in Nigeria's Fourth Republic (1999 to present), systematically shaping how citizens perceive candidates, parties, and democratic processes. This paper conceptually examines the relationship between electoral propaganda and public opinion formation in Nigeria, deploying Agenda-Setting Theory, the Propaganda Model, and the Spiral of Silence as an integrated analytical framework. Using a qualitative documentary approach based on the synthesis of scholarly and institutional sources, the study is organised around three thematic concerns: the structural machinery and media dimensions of electoral propaganda; the digital and AI-driven transformation of propaganda practice; and the implications of propaganda-saturated communication environments for democratic consolidation. The analysis demonstrates that electoral propaganda in Nigeria operates through coordinated information management, media capture, digital influence networks, and identity-based emotional appeals, producing public opinion climates that reflect elite preferences rather than deliberative citizen judgment. The findings further indicate that digital platforms, computational propaganda, organised disinformation networks, and emerging artificial intelligence applications have expanded the scale and sophistication of opinion manipulation in contemporary electoral politics. By integrating classical communication theories with emerging…

items.title: Bamboo Soil Carbon Sequestration and Climate Change Mitigation in Ethiopia
items.source_name: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
items.summary_raw: Bamboo ecosystems may contribute to climate change mitigation through the conservation of existing carbon stocks, recovery of carbon on degraded land, and storage or substitution benefits associated with harvested products. This critical narrative review examines Ethiopian evidence, emphasizing soil organic carbon (SOC), the distinction between carbon storage and sequestration, and priorities for future research. Twelve Ethiopia-focused publications and four international methodological or synthesis references were selected through targeted searches. Ethiopian studies document substantial SOC beneath both highland and lowland bamboo, but soil depths, land-use histories, analytical methods, and carbon pools differ markedly. Comparative evidence associates long-established highland bamboo with SOC stocks close to those of adjacent natural forest and above those of annual cropland, while a lowland conversion chronosequence indicates declining soil carbon following cultivation. These observations support conservation and justify testing restoration benefits; they do not establish a general annual sequestration rate. Predominantly cross-sectional designs, limited direct belowground measurements, and inconsistencies in some reported ecosystem totals restrict quantitative synthesis. Mechanisms involving litter inputs, roots, aggregation, and mineral association remain insufficiently resolved in Ethiopian bamboo systems. Priority research should combine repeated…

items.title: Plant growth promoting rhizobacteria and nanotechnology: emerging perspectives and functional roles for climate resilient sustainable agriculture
items.summary_raw: This review highlights the pivotal role of Plant Growth Promoting Rhizobacteria (PGPR) in association with nanotechnology for enhancing plant growth and health. It narratively discusses diverse PGPR groups and genera, outlining their direct mechanisms such as phosphate solubilization, nitrogen fixation, ACC deaminase activity, hydrogen cyanide production, and siderophore production for iron chelation as well as indirect mechanisms through induced systemic resistance (ISR) and systemic acquired resistance (SAR). The application of PGPR as single inoculants and in consortia, together with omics-based approaches, is examined to demonstrate their versatility in sustainable crop improvement. PGPR interactions with host plants, contributions to soil protection, and conditioning are also addressed. Despite their multifaceted benefits, limitations such as loss during aerial application or environmental stress remain challenges. Emerging nanotechnology-based delivery systems offer promising solutions by enabling controlled release of PGPR and their bioactive compounds, thereby targeting specific tissues and enhancing resilience under variable conditions. Collectively, this review underscores PGPR- mediated green nanotechnological strategies as eco- friendly alternatives to hazardous chemical inputs, advancing climate-resilient and sustainable agriculture.

items.title: Fifty years of statehood in Sikkim: beyond peace and progress – a lurking ecological crisis
items.summary_raw: In 2025, Sikkim celebrated the 50th anniversary of its Statehood with a great public spectacle, crafting a narrative of peace, prosperity, and successful assimilation into the Indian state. The commemoration event was effectively used to reproduce a collective sense of progress masking the increasing ecological crisis of the state. The article explores how Sikkim is discursively generated as an exceptional model state in the Northeast region, and how tourism-driven urbanisation, hydropower, and other infrastructure expansion increase the environmental vulnerability of the state. Drawing on media reports, policy narratives, and some of the key environmental episodes, the article shows how development imaginaries produce a spatio-temporal dialogue that enables infrastructure projects to be framed as the pinnacle of Sikkimese progress over the period. The article places Sikkim in the larger Eastern Himalayan ecological region and highlights changes brought about by climate change such as erratic rainfall, drying springs, forest fires, and an increased risk of Glacial Lake Outburst Floods (GLOFs). These issues are interpreted as structural warnings about the limitations of infrastructure-led development in a high-risk Himalayan ecosystem rather than as isolated crises or disasters.

items.title: Beyond degrees Celsius: Mapping competing justice scenarios in Australia's energy transition
items.summary_raw: The energy transition is routinely framed as a technical challenge. But transitions are socio-political undertakings. The struggle over what counts as a “just transition” is a struggle over what a liveable future should look like. Facts alone cannot settle this dilemma because the struggle rests on competing ideas about what a just transition is for . Detailed economic and physical scenarios map climate trajectories, but no comparable map exists of the internal rationales behind the transition narratives. Social science should fill that gap. This paper analyses public statements on the transition made in Australia between 2022 and 2025 by industry, government, think-tanks, civil-society and First Nations organisations. Using structuralist semiotic analysis, which reads each position as a structure of meaning built around a central opposition, we first construct five ideal-typical justice scenarios: Defensive Localism, Instrumental Accelerationism, Progressive Extractivism, Reformist Transition and Transformative Transition. The analysis reveals that each scenario has a structural blind spot: something it must ignore to remain internally consistent. We then draw an “Overton-Venn diagram” plotting the scenarios against two anchors that together form the contradiction all scenarios must manage: economic growth and biophysical planetary boundaries. The diagram shows that three of the scenarios treat growth and planetary boundaries as reconcilable, whereas Defensive Localism…

items.title: Transforming Canadian Federal Governance in a Polycrisis
items.summary_raw: Abstract Since 1995, scientific consensus has linked human activity to climate change, yet the political and financial power of the carbon economy remains entrenched. Under conditions of polycrisis, many states continue to miss emissions targets and, in some cases, retreat from climate commitments. Transformative political will is therefore urgently needed to achieve carbon neutrality. To examine constraints on federal climate action, we conducted interviews with 35 senior governance actors, including former public servants, environmental leaders, quasi‐institutional intermediaries (See footnote at the bottom of the page), and private sector advisors. Their experiences point to persistent governance barriers. Findings suggest the political process remains the primary constraint, shaped by short electoral cycles, policy reversals, limited public engagement, and entrenched financial power. We conceptualize these dynamics as limits to the governability of climate change, highlighting the need for stronger coordination, institutional capacity, and durable governance arrangements to sustain climate action under polycrisis conditions.

items.title: Economic advancement and environmental sustainability in the SADC region
items.summary_raw: This study investigates the long-run relationship between economic growth and ecological sustainability among member countries of the Southern African Development Community (SADC) between 1997 and 2021. The study employs heterogeneous dynamic panel estimation techniques, the Mean Group (MG) and Pooled Mean Group (PMG) estimators developed by M. Hashem Pesaran and Smith (1995) and Pesaran et al. (1999), while the Dynamic Fixed Effects (DFE) estimator is applied as a robustness check.To depict their appropriateness in capturing both short-run heterogeneity and long-run equilibrium correlations among countries. The results indicate statistically significant long-term connections between economic growth and various environmental metrics, such as per capita carbon dioxide emissions, emissions from electric and heat generation, industrial and construction emissions, total carbon emissions, and unemployment. The findings show a continuous long-term relationship between environmental and economic performance in the SADC subregion. Empirical analysis backs the Environmental Kuznets Curve (EKC) theory, suggesting that environmental destruction initially increases in the early phases of economic development but decreases after income reaches a certain higher level. Moreover, the findings support the ecological modernization theory, emphasising the capacity of cleaner technologies, especially renewable energy, to foster economic development while mitigating ecological damage…

items.title: LEGAL ANALYSIS OF RENEWABLE ENERGY AS A KEY STRATEGY FOR MITIGATING CLIMATE AND PROMOTING SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT IN NIGERIA
items.source_name: Journal of Jurisprudence, International Law and Contemporary Legal Issues
items.summary_raw: Nigeria with its abundant renewable energy potential, continues to rely heavenly on fossil fuels, which has slowed renewable energy deployment, contributing significantly to greenhouse gas emissions, environmental degradation, and developmental challenges, particularly climate change. These emissions are largely driven by energy production, industrial activities, and deforestation which has contributed to rising temperatures, extreme weather events, and ecological degradation. Although, Nigerian has numerous policies on renewable energy, progress towards clean energy remains slow due to weak, fragmented and poorly coordinated legal and institutional framework. This study provides a legal analysis of renewable energy as a strategic mechanism for climate change mitigation and sustainable development in Nigeria. The study critically analysis some existing national laws and policies, on renewable energy and relevant provisions of environmental and electricity sector regulations, to assess their effectiveness in mitigating climate change and promoting sustainable development. Using a doctrinal legal research methodology, the study identifies gaps such as low utilization of renewable energy resources due to the absence of a comprehensive renewable legal framework, weak enforcement of renewable energy policies, regulatory overlaps, inadequate integration of renewable energy into national development planning. It argues that strengthening legal and institutional frameworks is…
