items.title: Public responses to biodiversity loss terminology and crisis framing
items.summary_raw: To avoid the technical term "biodiversity loss", public communications often refer to "nature loss" or "extinction of plants and animals" or apply crisis framing by stating "biodiversity crisis," "nature crisis," or "extinction crisis." To assess public responses to these terms, we conducted a randomized survey experiment with 7338 U.S. adults. Participants were randomly assigned to one term (biodiversity loss, nature loss, extinction of plants and animals, biodiversity crisis, nature crisis, or extinction crisis), either alone or in the context of an explanation and photos of plants and animals. With and without context, "biodiversity loss" and "biodiversity crisis" received the lowest ratings of familiarity, concern, perceived urgency, and conservation support. "Extinction of plants and animals" generally received the highest ratings. "Nature loss" performed similarly to this term when context was provided. Crisis framing had little to no effect. Terminology effects were strongest for political Independents. We discuss implications for public communications.

items.title: The circulation and water mass (trans)formations in the Arctic Mediterranean Sea and their implications for the deep ocean circulation: a narrative
items.summary_raw: Abstract. The Arctic Mediterranean is rapidly changing, a statement that is often made, but the follow-up statements: changing from what and towards what are often omitted. Hence its role in the global climate system, particularly regarding the Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulations remains poorly constrained. This review of the oceanography of the Arctic Mediterranean Sea develops an unified perspective of how interacting components of the system evolve in space and time, and the processes that determine their evolution. To set the stage a succinct overview of the geographic setting and early explorations is given. We then follow the pathways of the principal water masses to describe inflows, inter-basin circulations, water mass transformations, and outflows of heat and salt to the bordering subpolar gyre and the global ocean. The fundamental connection to the global ocean, the Atlantic water, is traced along its route into and through the Arctic Mediterranean. Its transformations, driven by cooling, and by the freezing and melting of sea ice, lead to the creation of both denser and less dense waters that form and maintain the water column structures within the Arctic Mediterranean; the so-called double estuary. A second advective component to the Arctic, the low salinity water carried by the Pacific inflow, is concentrated into the Amerasian Basin and acts there to further isolate the denser waters derived from the Atlantic inflow. Hence, the waters return to the…

items.title: Climate change impacts on water resources and SDG implementation in East Africa with a focus on Ethiopia a workshop report on adaptation strategies
items.summary_raw: This workshop was organized to identify strategies for advancing the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) under a changing climate, with a focus on building resilience and promoting sustainable water management in Ethiopia. The workshop format combined academic presentations, group discussions, and a field excursion to a botanic reserve park showcasing successful SDG interventions. A carefully selected group of DAAD Alumni, representing diverse academic disciplines, professional levels (ranging from professors to undergraduates), and geographic regions across the country, convened for a two-day intensive session. Participants drew on their experiences and local realities to deliberate on five thematic areas identified through in-depth literature review and consultations with academic mentors. Key outcomes include eight strategic recommendations: (1) strengthening climate-resilient water storage and management; (2) transforming agriculture through efficient water use and climate-smart practices; (3) expanding renewable energy integration; (4) empowering communities and local innovations; (5) strengthening integrated policies and institutional coordination; (6) enhancing data and climate information services; (7) unlocking climate finance and carbon markets; and (8) protecting ecosystems through nature-based solutions. These outputs offer actionable strategies for policymakers and practitioners to build climate resilience and accelerate SDG progress in Ethiopia and across East…

items.title: Enhancing Agricultural Resilience Through Climate-Smart Practices: A Case Study of Smallholder Farmers in Horro Guduru Wallaga Zone, Hababo Guduru Woreda
items.source_name: International Journal of Economy Energy and Environment
items.summary_raw: Climate variability and environmental stressors, including erratic rainfall, recurrent drought, and soil degradation, increasingly threaten the sustainability of smallholder agriculture in Ethiopia, where rain-fed farming remains the main source of livelihood and food security. Although climate-smart agriculture (CSA) is widely promoted as a strategy to increase productivity, build resilience, and reduce greenhouse gas emissions, evidence on its effects at the local level remains limited. This study therefore investigates how CSA practices enhance the resilience of smallholder farmers in Hababo Guduru Woreda, Horro Guduru Wallaga Zone, and Oromia Regional State, Ethiopia. A mixed-methods research design was employed, combining quantitative and qualitative approaches. Primary data were collected through household surveys, key informant interviews, and focus group discussions with smallholder farmers, development agents, and local officials. Quantitative data were analysed using descriptive and inferential statistics, while qualitative data were analysed thematically. The findings reveal that the adoption of CSA practices, such as soil and water conservation, improved crop varieties, agroforestry, crop diversification, and organic fertilizer use, improves crop productivity, soil health, and household food security while reducing vulnerability to climate shocks. Policy support, farmer training and extension services, and access to financial incentives and credit were identified…

items.title: Joining the dots: why more and accurate media coverage of climate change matters
News reporting on arrests and trials of climate activists in the U.S., U.K., and Sweden
items.summary_raw: Abstract This paper examines how news media textually and visually represented the protests, arrests, and criminal trials of climate activists in the U.S., U.K., and Sweden during the early-2020s—a period of heightened anti-climate reactionary backlash in response to the progressive and transnational climate movement of the 2010s. This study’s cross-national, comparative, and multimodal critical discourse analysis reveals a privileging of police and prosecutors’ accounts as the primary—and oftentimes final— definers, with little room given to protesters to contest their criminalization. The analysis highlights differences between media and countries in addition to overarching patterns. Ultimately, this paper shows how major news outlets across all three countries gave primary voice to elite figures from the state’s legal apparatus to discredit protesters, but also, in the U.K. and Sweden, how these figures were occasionally qualified by scientific, political, and other experts in defense of activists—a trend strikingly absent from U.S. outlets.

items.title: A LiDAR-driven urban energy benchmarking framework for mapping building energy intensity and carbon emissions in hyper-arid cities
items.summary_raw: Abstract Rapid urbanization and intensifying heat extremes are accelerating building energy demand and associated carbon emissions in hyper-arid cities. However, quantifying building-level energy performance at high spatial resolution remains challenging because building morphology, floor area, and energy-consumption data are rarely integrated within a comprehensive framework. This study develops an integrated geospatial framework that integrates LiDAR-derived three-dimensional building morphology, high-resolution building footprints, and electricity-consumption data to quantify building-level energy use intensity (EUI), operational carbon emissions, and energy-performance patterns across Qatar. LiDAR-derived building morphology, deep-learning-based building footprints from high-resolution Pléiades imagery, and 14,186 electricity meter records were integrated with forest-based regression to estimate EUI across the mapped building stock. The analysis reveals pronounced sectoral and spatial disparities in building energy performance. Residential villas account for 35.5% of estimated operational building carbon emissions, while commercial, industrial, and governmental buildings collectively contribute 56.02%. Between 2020 and 2024, electricity consumption increased by 8.52% in the residential sector and by 25.0% in commercial and industrial buildings. Annual ean EUI rose from 158 ± 15 to 206 ± 20 kWh/m 2 , and total operational CO 2 -equivalent emissions increased from 19.3 to…

items.title: Climate Change as a Chronic Stressor: Biological and Psychological Pathways Linking Environmental Change to Human Well-Being
items.summary_raw: Climate-related hazards are associated with adverse mental and physical health outcomes, but exposure-specific human findings are often discussed together with general stress mechanisms without clearly distinguishing their evidentiary strength. This narrative review addresses that gap by examining climate change as a context for recurrent thermal, disaster-related, and psychosocial stress, rather than as a single measurable exposure. Evidence is organized around three interacting biological domains: neuroendocrine regulation, inflammation and oxidative stress, and neuroplasticity. Human observational studies support associations between heat, extreme events, and mental health outcomes; short-term human experiments and animal models provide mechanistic insights but do not establish a chronic biological mediation pathway from climate change to psychiatric illness. Indirect pathways include displacement, livelihood disruption, loss, and anticipatory distress. Air pollution is treated as an interacting exposure with both climate-related and independent determinants. Eco-anxiety, climate anxiety, eco-distress, and ecological grief are distinguished from diagnosable disorders, with clinical relevance assessed through functional impairment and individual context. The review’s contribution is an evidence-qualified framework linking exposure timing, biological plausibility, psychosocial appraisal, and unequal adaptive capacity. Practical implications include contextual mental health…

items.title: ‘We don't do politics’: theorizing climate change communication on Australian community radio through radical eco-communicative democracy
items.summary_raw: In times of disaster and in grappling with the slower, more insidious changes to daily life, community radio has a vital yet undervalued role to play in supporting community resilience to climate change. However, approaches across Australia's large and diverse community broadcasting sector are as varied as the stations themselves. While there are stations actively engaging with climate change and leading their communities’ responses, there are even more stations hesitant to start. Drawing on research conducted with 12 community radio stations across two Australian states, this article explores the reluctance of some community radio stations to get involved in what they see as the ‘political’ issue of climate change. By viewing these findings and the broader work of Australia's community radio sector through a framework of radical eco-communicative democracy, it is possible to chart a path that moves beyond politicization and towards meaningful community-led conversations about climate change.

items.title: Understanding user archetypes in fully autonomous vehicle adoption: insights from factor-based clustering
items.summary_raw: Fully autonomous vehicles (FAVs) are expected to render the driving environment safer and eco-friendlier, but their widespread adoption is highly dependent on the public’s acceptance. This study aimed to identify the key factors that impact perceptions of FAVs by surveying prospective users in Arlington, Texas, and evaluating the range of attitudinal and behavioral variables associated with the psychological and social determinants of receptivity to FAVs. An exploratory factor analysis classified primary acceptance of FAVs, anxiety about FAVs, driving enjoyment, and intrinsic trust in AVs as the four main factors of FAV adoption. The results from the factor analysis were analyzed using cluster analysis and identified the following three discrete classes: tech-trusting skeptics (34% of the sample), traditional drivers (37%), and pragmatic adopters (29%). The findings of this study describe the user archetypes of FAV adopters and discuss the importance of designing public policies that ensure a smooth transition from partially-to-FAVs.

items.title: The Battleground Districts Where Electricity Bills Have Surged the Most

The 15th wealthiest congressional district in the country, NJ-7 stretches from the tidal strait bordering New York’s Staten Island to the winding Delaware River state line with Pennsylvania. Between those two bodies of water, roughly a third of households earn more than $200,000 a year. The 7th Congressional District is also New Jersey’s “one rare and surprising swing district,” per Gothamist , and, as a result, it is also the spendiest on elections: the 2024 high-water mark of $26.3 million in campaign spending will likely be surpassed this year by incumbent Republican Tom Kean Jr. and Democrat Rebecca Bennett. Needless to say, there are comparatively few constituents in NJ-7 for whom paying $40 more on a September electricity bill than two years ago — or about $300 more over the past 12 months — is the difference between whether they can afford groceries or not . But like many other Republican-held competitive seats this election year, the district has seen its electricity rates increase since just before President Donald Trump took office for his second term, according to the latest data available in Heatmap and MIT’s Electricity Price Hub . In NJ-7, residents paid about 35% more on their electricity bills this September than two years ago; bills are up more than 18% over the past 12 months compared with the year before. items.title: Widespread plasma jets in the Martian magnetosheath revealed by dual-spacecraft observations
items.summary_raw: Plasma jets in planetary magnetosheaths are transient, high dynamic pressure structures capable of strongly perturbing downstream magnetospheres and modulating solar wind energy transfer. Although recently identified at Mars, their formation mechanisms and global occurrence remain poorly constrained. Using dual-spacecraft observations from Mars Atmosphere and Volatile EvolutioN and Tianwen-1, we show that magnetosheath jets occur throughout the Martian magnetosheath, in striking contrast to Earth where jet occurrence is strongly controlled by interplanetary magnetic field orientation and largely confined to quasi-parallel shock regions. We propose that this widespread distribution is linked to Mars’ extended hydrogen corona, which generates pickup ions that drive proton-cyclotron waves upstream of the bow shock. Because this mechanism is generic to any body with an extended corona (or exosphere) embedded in a stellar wind, this finding bears on solar–wind interactions at comets and other small bodies, and on the space environments of unmagnetized terrestrial exoplanets. These results indicate that magnetosheath jet formation can be governed not only by external solar wind forcing but also by intrinsic planetary properties, pointing to a previously unrecognized pathway for solar wind–planet coupling at unmagnetized worlds.

items.title: Evolution of the arbuscular mycorrhizal regulatory network through differential GRAS gene retention and protein interaction in land plants
items.summary_raw: Plants rely on an ancient genetic “toolkit” to establish arbuscular mycorrhizal symbiosis (AMS) with fungal partners. However, the symbiotic outcomes vary among AMS hosts, indicating divergence in downstream transcriptional reprogramming after the perception of symbiotic signals. To uncover the cross-species variation of the AMS regulatory network, we traced the evolutionary trajectory of the GRAS gene family, which encodes the major group of transcription factors in AMS regulation. Phylogenetic analysis of the GRAS family across land plants placed known symbiotic GRAS members within 12 anciently diverged lineages, with multiple lineages showing pronounced gene loss in nonmycorrhizal plants. This pattern pointed to three additional GRAS lineages as candidates for AMS regulation. Given that tomato harbors single-copy, AMS-induced genes in these lineages, we selected it for functional validation. CRISPR-Cas9 mutagenesis, combined with detailed phenotyping of fungal colonization and arbuscule morphology, and transcriptome profiling of mutant roots, confirmed that all three tomato genes are individually required for AMS development, designated Symbiosis-Required GRAS (SRG) 1 to 3. Large-scale phylogenomic analysis and protein interaction assays (by yeast two-hybrid and bimolecular fluorescence complementation) further showed that both the repertoire and interaction networks of symbiotic GRAS members vary among AMS hosts. In summary, together with 12 previously characterized…

items.title: Harnessing autoantibodies to target pathogenic plasma cells
PSF3 recruits Polθ to stalled replication forks to promote DNA repair
items.summary_raw: DNA polymerase theta (Polθ) plays a pivotal role in the maintenance of stalled replication forks. However, little is known about how Polθ is recruited to the stalled forks. Here we show that PSF3, a member of GINS replicative complex, recruits Polθ to the stalled replication forks. Polθ, which is recruited by interacting with the C-terminal portion of PSF3, restarts the forks, exerts DNA double-strand break end-joining to repair the breaks resulting from collapsed forks in BRCA1/2-deficient and proficient tumor cells, and also fills single-stranded gaps on the replication fork lagging strand in BRCA1/2-deficient tumor cells. Thus, PSF3–Polθ interaction promotes the proliferation of homologous recombination-deficient and proficient tumor cells. Overall, this study highlights an important mechanism of Polθ recruitment to the stalled replication forks to maintain Polθ-dependent fork protection in tumor cells.

items.title: Mediator-associated proteins and the small RNA–guided Polycomb repressive complex enhance cryptic transcription for transposon exclusion
items.summary_raw: Suppression of transposable elements (TEs) is critical for maintaining genome integrity. The evolutionary arms race between TEs and their eukaryotic host organisms has driven the development of small RNA–dependent mechanisms that specifically suppress TEs while leaving non-TE regions unperturbed. In the binucleated ciliate Tetrahymena , small RNAs (sRNAs) are generated from both TE and non-TE regions of the germline genome, whereas noncoding RNAs (ncRNAs) from the TE-free somatic genome target and eliminate non-TE sRNAs, thereby selectively preserving TE-specific sRNAs for guiding TE recognition. Since sRNAs are produced from both strands, the counteracting ncRNAs must also occur bidirectionally. However, the mechanism by which the somatic genome generates ncRNAs from both strands remains unresolved. Here, we show that these ncRNAs arise from widespread cryptic transcription initiated outside canonical promoters and dependent on the developmentally specific Mediator complex–associated proteins Dima1 and Emit2. We further demonstrate that sRNA-guided recruitment of the Tetrahymena Polycomb repressive complex 2 and Dima1 occupancy are mutually reinforcing, promoting local accumulation of RNA polymerase II, which may facilitate cryptic transcription from these loci in a histone methyltransferase-independent manner. Disruption of Dima1 abolishes cryptic transcription, leads to aberrant accumulation of non-TE sRNAs, and results in erroneous genome elimination and cell death…

items.title: A tunable immune-evasion function of Zika virus NS5 governs viral fitness and pathogenesis
items.summary_raw: Type I interferon (IFN) signaling is a central antiviral defense, with STAT2 driving the expression of IFN-stimulated genes (ISGs) to restrict viral infection. Zika virus (ZIKV) and dengue virus evade this pathway through nonstructural protein 5 (NS5)-mediated ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation of STAT2, yet the contribution of this immune-evasion strategy to viral fitness and pathogenesis remains incompletely defined. Here, using a multistep mutational scanning strategy that jointly assessed STAT2 degradation and viral RNA replication, we identified a single NS5 residue, L162, as uniquely permissive to substitution that abolishes STAT2 degradation without compromising intrinsic replication functions. Substitution of L162 with alanine or glycine (L162A or L162G) selectively disrupted NS5 recruitment of the ZSWIM8-CUL3 E3 ubiquitin ligase, thereby preserving STAT2 stability and restoring IFN signaling. Recombinant ZIKV carrying these mutations exhibited reduced replication and enhanced ISG induction in human cells, defects fully rescued by STAT2 knockout. In A129 mice (type I IFN receptor deficient), mutant and WT viruses replicated comparably, but in human STAT2 knock-in mice, ZIKV-NS5 L162G exhibited markedly reduced viral loads and disease. In pregnant human STAT2 knock-in mice, the mutant also reduced placental and fetal viral burdens and adverse pregnancy outcomes. Notably, infection with ZIKV-NS5 L162G elicited robust neutralizing antibody and T cell responses…

items.title: Molecular basis for discrimination of cGAMP linkage isomers by a c-di-GMP-II riboswitch variant
items.summary_raw: Riboswitches are noncoding RNA regulatory motifs predominantly found in bacteria. Signaling molecules such as c-di-GMP, c-di-AMP, and 3′,3′-cGAMP have been reported to be recognized by riboswitches. In contrast, 2′,3′-cGAMP functions as a second messenger in mammalian cells, yet its interaction with RNA molecules remains unclear. Here, we report the crystal structures of a c-di-GMP-II riboswitch variant, c-di-GMP-II-Bh, bound to 2′,3′-cGAMP and 3′,3′-cGAMP. Both complexes adopt a similar overall RNA scaffold with an identical binding pocket composition. However, the ligand bases adopt inverted orientations in the binding pocket, resulting in distinct interaction patterns with residues A64 and G68 and differences in base-pair stacking against the phosphodiester backbone. Structural comparison together with ligand-binding assays of structure-guided mutants using isothermal titration calorimetry reveals the molecular principles by which an RNA riboswitch discriminates among cyclic dinucleotide linkage isomers, highlighting the remarkable sensitivity of RNA binding pockets to subtle ligand structural variations and provides a mechanistic framework for understanding ligand specificity in RNA–small molecule recognition.

items.title: Gut microbiota vesicle reprogramming by Ganoderma lucidum polysaccharide alleviates mycoplasmal pneumonia via the gut–lung axis
items.summary_raw: Respiratory infections remain a major global health challenge, further compounded by antibiotic resistance. Among these, mycoplasmal pneumonia represents a particularly prevalent and refractory form. Here, using targeted enzymatic fragmentation combined with multidimensional NMR analysis, we resolved the structure of a homogeneous Ganoderma lucidum polysaccharide, GLFP2, and identified β-(1→6)-linked galactosyl motifs as key structural features. Despite minimal systemic absorption, oral GLFP2 alleviated mycoplasmal pneumonia in mice. Instead, GLFP2 reshaped the gut microbiota and functionally reprogrammed gut microbiota-derived extracellular vesicles (GMEVs), whose transplantation alone was sufficient to confer pulmonary protection. Orally administered GMEVs remained bioactive, showed systemic exposure, associated with the lung, and were preferentially taken up by alveolar macrophages. These vesicles activated AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK) signaling, suppressed the S100A8/A9 inflammatory axis, and limited neutrophil-driven immunopathology. Collectively, these findings identify microbiota-derived vesicles as effectors of gut–lung communication and use a defined polysaccharide to uncover a remote protective mechanism against pneumonia.

items.title: Transient ATM inhibition enhances knock-in efficiency in hematopoietic stem cells by attenuating the DNA damage response
items.summary_raw: Precise genome editing in hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs) holds great potential for treating inherited blood disorders; however, low knock-in (KI) efficiency and loss of functional HSCs after genome editing remain major obstacles. Here, we demonstrate that transient inhibition of Ataxia-Telangiectasia Mutated (ATM) kinase markedly enhanced KI efficiency in mouse HSCs genome-edited with Cas9/ribonucleoprotein (RNP) and AAV donor DNA. Phosphoproteomic and capillary western blot analyses revealed that ATM inhibition suppressed aberrant Cas9-AAV-induced ATM activation and the subsequent DNA damage response, reduced p53-dependent apoptosis, and enhanced survival of KI HSCs. In serial transplantation assays, ATM inhibition preserved long-term engrafting KI HSCs, increasing their frequency from ~0.3 to 40% in secondary recipients, an over 100-fold improvement. Furthermore, in an X-linked severe combined immunodeficient mouse model, ATM inhibition increased KI efficiency and restored T- and B cell differentiation. Comprehensive safety analyses, including long-read nanopore sequencing, amplicon deep sequencing, whole genome sequencing and clonal tracking, did not detect increased genomic alterations, chromosomal abnormalities, or clonal expansion following transient ATM inhibition. Taken together, these findings establish transient ATM inhibition as an effective strategy to enhance KI-mediated genome editing while maintaining the long-term repopulating capacity of HSCs.

items.title: Meta-analysis of 990 EBV genomes identifies EBER2 SNP7048 and its interaction with HLA-A*11:01 driving nasopharyngeal carcinoma risk
items.summary_raw: Nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC) is a major health burden in East and Southeast Asia (SEA). While EBV infection is a primary driver, the specific viral strains responsible for NPC development and their interaction with host genetics across geographically diverse endemic regions remain poorly understood. We performed a whole-genome sequencing of 388 EBV isolates and matched host whole-exome sequencing in a Singaporean cohort. To define the global significance of these findings, we conducted a meta-GWAS and phylogenetic analysis across three independent cohorts (Singapore, Hong Kong, and Guangdong and Guangxi provinces of China), totaling 990 EBV genomes. Our study identifies high-risk EBV strains—carrying a core variant in the EBER2 locus (SNP7048)—as the key viral determinator of NPC risk, accounting for approximately 68% of the attributable risk in SEA. Meta-analysis reveals these strains are consistently associated with NPC across all populations, resolving previous regional genetic discordances. We demonstrate a potent synergistic interaction between these EBV risk strains and the host HLA-A*11:01 protective allele; individuals lacking this protection while carrying a high-risk strain exhibit a 30.9-fold increase in NPC risk. Phylogenetic analysis further reveals that these high-risk lineages populated SEA through clonal expansion from Southern China, following historical migration routes. These findings establish that NPC development is driven by the distribution of…

items.title: CX3CL1 (fractalkine)–CX3CR1 interface drives CD8⁺ T cell–induced neurodegeneration in human brain organoids
items.summary_raw: Immune–neuron interactions play a critical role in neuroinflammatory and neurodegenerative diseases, such as Alzheimer’s disease (AD), but how CD8⁺ T cells contribute to brain pathology remains poorly understood. Amyloid-β (Aβ), a hallmark of AD, is known to trigger neuronal stress and inflammation. Here, we established a human cortical organoid (hCO) model to investigate CD8⁺ T cell responses to Aβ-induced neurodegenerative stress. Aβ exposure increased neuronal expression of CX3CL1 (fractalkine), which engages its receptor CX3CR1 on CD8⁺ T cells. Transwell migration assays showed enhanced recruitment of CX3CR1⁺ CD8⁺ T cells toward Aβ-treated hCOs. In parallel, Aβ upregulated IL-15 expression, a cytokine that supports CD8⁺ T cell activation. The infiltration of CD8⁺ T cells led to neuronal injury, marked by MAP2 loss and cleaved Caspase-3 activation, accompanied by an increase in gene signatures for cell death and inflammation. Exposure to the conditioned medium of activated CX3CR1 high CD8⁺ T cell recapitulated this damage, and the neutralization of CD8 + T cell cytokines and cytotoxic molecules rescued the phenotype. These findings identify the CX3CL1–CX3CR1 axis and CD8⁺ T cell effector programs as drivers of neurotoxicity and establish brain organoids as a platform to study immune-driven neurodegeneration.

items.title: Screw dislocation–mediated galaxy-mimicking superspiral assembly with amplified bio-piezoelectricity
items.summary_raw: From the galaxies to the petals, spiral architectures are ubiquitous to confer hierarchical organizations, supporting asymmetric galactic evolutions and biological activities. Herein, inspired from nature, we report the superspiral architectures self-assembled by a minimalist amino acid. These superspirals, with spirality and geometry programmably tuned by enantiomeric excess and organization parameters, are determined to arise from the screw dislocation induced hierarchical crystallization. Notably, the spiral organization can integrate and amplify electrical polarization, yielding 17-fold enhancement in piezoelectric response contrast to random aggregates. This allows engineering of piezoelectric bioelectronics, resulting in high gain direction-selective motion sensing. Our work establishes an alternative paradigm for developing bioinspired hierarchical architectures of oriented and amplified properties, offering a self-assembling route to explore programmably modulated functional architectures for bioelectronic engineering.

items.title: Programmable chemoenzymatic synthesis of a keratan sulfate N -glycan library for glycocode decoding
items.summary_raw: Keratan sulfate (KS) is a unique and widely distributed glycosaminoglycans family implicated in diverse biological processes. KS features branched glycan architectures with diverse sialylation and sulfation patterns, encoding a vastly expanded chemical and biological space. The limited accessibility of well-defined structures has hindered precise investigations into the KS biological functions. Here we report a programmable chemoenzymatic platform for assembling a 106-membered library of KS N -glycans and their nonsulfated counterparts, featuring length-variable oligo- N -acetyllactosamine (LacNAc) extensions and encompassing diverse sulfation and sialylation patterns. The synthetic strategy integrates length-controlled iterative glycosylation to assemble versatile precursors, orthogonal deprotection for site-specific sulfation, and modular enzyme-driven diversification. Glycan microarray analysis of this comprehensive library reveals that glycan–protein recognition is governed by the interplay of sulfation and sialylation patterns, oligo-LacNAc chain length, and terminal epitope presentation, providing insight into the functional versatility of KS glycans.

items.title: Causality in liquid water as a hallmark of emergent glassy dynamics
items.summary_raw: In molecular liquids such as water, time-delayed influences between microscopic or mesoscopic variables are typically probed using time-correlation functions, which are symmetric under detailed balance and therefore blind to dynamical asymmetries. Here, we characterize water’s dynamics using a causal inference metric that captures asymmetric couplings between collective variables. Analyzing equilibrium molecular dynamics simulations at ambient conditions and in the high-density liquid (HDL) regime of supercooled water, we uncover pronounced asymmetries in the couplings between orientational and translational degrees of freedom across multiple time and length scales. At room temperature, rotational modes exert a modest directional influence on translational dynamics. In contrast, in the supercooled HDL regime, translational motions emerge as the primary drivers of the dynamics, suggesting facilitation-like relaxation mechanisms characteristic of glassy systems. These results reveal a qualitative reorganization of dynamical couplings across thermodynamic conditions, implying that molecular liquids at thermal equilibrium can exhibit an emergent directionality in their fluctuation couplings. As a consequence, our analysis reveals that external perturbations acting on specific degrees of freedom can induce a stronger arrow of time in the causal relations between translational and orientational modes.

items.title: Conformational flexibility of the nitrogenase-like reductase CfbC/D involved in coenzyme F 430 biosynthesis
items.summary_raw: The nitrogenase-like reductase CfbC/D catalyzes the six-electron reduction of the tetrapyrrole macrocycle of Ni 2+ -sirohydrochlorin a,c -diamide during the biosynthesis of coenzyme F 430 , an essential cofactor for biological methane formation and consumption. The individual dimeric protein components, CfbC 2 and CfbD 2 , form a complex to allow for electron transfer from the [4Fe:4S] cluster in CfbC 2 to the [4Fe:4S] cluster in CfbD 2 and onto the substrate. The overall process is ATP-dependent. Although CfbC/D belongs to the family of nitrogenase-like enzymes, there are several intriguing differences between CfbC/D, other nitrogenase-like enzymes and nitrogenase itself. In contrast to the other enzymes, CfbC/D exhibits a simpler molecular architecture, forming a heterotetrameric CfbC 2 D 2 assembly. Furthermore, the interaction of the CfbC and CfbD components does not depend on the presence of adenosine triphosphate (ATP). Here we report cryoelectron microscopy structures of the CfbC/D complex prepared in the absence and presence of substrates. These structures not only shed light on the molecular architecture of the CfbC/D complex but also reveal a high degree of structural flexibility within the CfbD 2 component, which undergoes a large conformational change in the presence of an ATP analog and the tetrapyrrole substrate. The interplay of CfbD with its reductase CfbC also strongly suggests an evolutionary pathway toward the modern nitrogenase from methanogenic archaea.

items.title: Mechanism of HIV-1 capsid rupture and uncoating by reverse transcription
items.summary_raw: One of the key events in the HIV-1 life cycle is reverse transcription (RT), during which single-stranded viral RNA (ssRNA) is converted into double-stranded DNA (dsDNA). This process occurs inside the mature HIV-1 capsid and, once it reaches a critical threshold, drives capsid rupture. This uncoating is essential for infection because it releases viral genetic material into the host cell nucleus. Despite its importance, many mechanistic details of this process remain to be fully understood. To address this gap, we develop a multiscale computational method for simulating RT inside the capsid, termed Coarse-Grained Kinetic Monte Carlo (CG-KMC). CG-KMC stochastically adds deoxynucleotide triphosphates (dNTPs) to the coarse-grained RNA model, enabling stepwise growth of DNA inside the HIV-1 capsid. We implement this method within an integrative coarse-grained framework that combines a “bottom-up” capsid model with a “top-down” representation of the viral RNA/DNA genome. Our simulations phenomenologically capture and predict diverse capsid rupture pathways during RT. The resulting ruptured structures closely match previously identified cryo-ET images. We further perform an extensive analysis of the rupture process, examining its mechanistic and kinetic aspects as well as the role of capsid–DNA interactions. Our findings illuminate how different capsid–DNA conditions give rise to distinct rupture pathways, which differ from ruptures due to simple outward pressure expansion models…

items.title: Methanogenic archaea Methanobrevibacter smithii and Methanosphaera stadtmanae promote mucosal homeostasis and protect from colitis
items.summary_raw: The intestinal microbiota is a critical determinant of mucosal homeostasis, yet the functional contributions of Archaea—which constitute up to 10% of the anaerobic community—remain largely undefined. Here, we provide evidence that the human methanogens Methanobrevibacter smithii (MSm) and Methanosphaera stadtmanae (MSt) promote colonic health. Transcriptomic analysis of germ-free mice reveals that MSm and MSt induce distinct colonic programs important for epithelial integrity. Using gnotobiotic and antibiotic-treated specific-pathogen-free mouse models, we show that MSm and MSt reinforce the epithelial barrier, characterized by increased goblet cell expansion, mucus thickening, and enhanced epithelial regeneration. Furthermore, methanogens expand Foxp3 + regulatory T cell (T reg ) populations without inducing pro-inflammatory T H 17 responses. Notably, MSm and MSt protect against dextran sodium sulfate-induced colitis. While MSt-mediated protection requires adaptive immunity, MSm retains partial efficacy in lymphocyte-deficient mice, revealing nonredundant protective mechanisms. These findings indicate that methanogenic archaea promote mucosal integrity during host association and suggest that methanogens may hold therapeutic potential for inflammatory bowel disease, though translation to human disease remains to be established.

items.title: Magnetically guided programmable thermomechanical protection enabled by biomimetic asymmetric design
items.summary_raw: Precision instruments operating in harsh environments require protective materials that can dissipate impact energy while resisting heat. However, actively tunable thermomechanical protection under coupled multiphysics conditions remains challenging. Inspired by shellfish and echinoderms, here we show that an asymmetrically engineered shear-stiffening gel (SSG) yields a Janus magnetorheological elastomer whose two faces mimic the brick-and-mortar architecture of shellfish and the impact-hardening behavior of echinoderms, respectively. Unlike single-modification anti-creep strategies of SSG that degrade shear-stiffening or severely increase initial modulus, our design achieves a 40-fold mechanical tunability, with the storage modulus ranging from 11.29 to 450.28 kPa, arising from the synergistic enhancement of strain-rate-dependent stiffening and magnetic interactions. The integration of magnetic and optical functions enables semiactive noncontact 2D-to-3D protection, achieving an 85% reduction in impact force and a 40 °C temperature difference via bidirectional photothermal regulation, demonstrating competitive thermomechanical protection performance. Furthermore, this strategy establishes a magnetically guided programmable pathway for thermomechanical protection and provides a generalizable blueprint for multifunctional intelligent materials, advancing protective technologies for outdoor equipment operating in extreme environments involving coupled physical fields.

items.title: Bridging spatial scales in respiratory viral infection
items.summary_raw: Respiratory viruses spread within the host through a combination of local expansion and occasional long-range dissemination that seeds new infection foci. We present LEAP (Lotka-Euler Airway Pathogen model), an analytically tractable within-host model that captures this two-scale process. The model takes the form of an age-dependent branching process and yields a closed-form expression for the exponential growth rate during early infection. Using empirical data to parameterize the model, we find that productive dissemination requires only a small number of successful long-range seeding events per infected cell, with distinct values for SARS-CoV-2 and influenza A virus. LEAP further predicts that, in these well-adapted viruses, interferon-mediated restriction only weakly affects exponential growth, while remaining decisive for poorly adapted pathogens. More broadly, the model provides a flexible framework for experimentally testable predictions of early infection dynamics.

items.title: Disentangling the evolving effects of climate change and technology diffusion on building electricity demand
items.summary_raw: Climate change and technology diffusion will jointly drive future growth in building electricity demand. How this nonadditive response evolves over time with the pace of climate change and technology diffusion has not previously been examined, despite its importance for maintaining reliable power systems. We estimate electricity demand from residential and commercial buildings under climate change and/or technology diffusion across 183 counties in the United States through 2060. Our framework drives 209,352 machine learning models of building electricity demand with 100 spatiotemporally downscaled climate realizations across four climate models and three emissions scenarios, and 18 technology diffusion pathways of air source heat pumps and insulation. We find that the combined response of peak demand to climate change and technology diffusion diverges substantially from the sum of their individual responses, with distinct patterns across hot and cold grid regions. In cold regions, climate change and technology diffusion drive roughly up to 10 times larger peak demand growth than climate change alone by 2060. Conversely, in hot regions, technology diffusion counteracts climate-change-driven peak demand growth. Across regions, climate-change-induced warming reduces or eliminates a shift toward winter peaking driven by technology diffusion. Via uncertainty partitioning, we find climate-related uncertainty dominates near-term peak demand uncertainty, while…

items.title: Connexins are essential for the contribution of latent progenitors to healing after spinal cord injury
items.summary_raw: Gap junctions are important regulators of the biology of neural stem cells. Both in vertebrates with regenerative abilities and neonatal rodents, ependymal cells communicate via connexin (Cx) 43 and Cx26. Gap junction coupling and Cx26 are down-regulated as the ependyma becomes quiescent in adulthood, but injury overrules this developmental down-regulation suggesting a role for Cx signaling in the reactivation of ependymal cells. However, direct evidence of the involvement of these Cxs in the reactivation of the ependymal stem cell niche is lacking. Here, we aim to explore the role of Cx26 and Cx43 in the response of ependymal cells to injury by means of specific genetic deletion. We find that Cx26 is critical for the proliferative response of ependymal cells to injury. The reduced response of ependymal cells by Cx26 deletion increased the extension of the lesion because of impaired healing resulting from a weak contribution of the ependymal stem cell niche. On the other hand, Cx43—via gap junction coupling and hemichannels—plays a key role in the communication of Ca 2+ signals between ependymal cells induced by activation of P2X7 receptors. Our data show that Cxs are relevant targets to manipulate the ependymal stem cell niche to achieve better healing after spinal cord injury.

items.title: Multiple sources contribute to predictive tactile attenuation in the mouse whisker system
items.summary_raw: The brain predicts action outcomes using interacting neuronal systems that integrate sensory feedback, movement, and rewards. In the mouse whisker system, we investigated whether two presumed predictive mechanisms jointly attenuate ascending tactile signals during movement. To this end, we employed an open-loop whisker-reach task that monitored facial nucleus motor activity and presented experimental tactile consequences while measuring tactile attenuation in the barrel cortex. Experimentally manipulating sensory consequences revealed two distinct systems. Sensory gating, a previously documented but functionally unclear mechanism of tactile attenuation, appeared graded but persisted during and after movement. In contrast, a second system was found to be temporally precise, generate suppression when stimuli are omitted, and capable of being learned within hundreds of trials. We label it state estimation as its characteristics—active suppression of expected tactile input—aligns well with the classical reafference principle, previously overlooked in the whisker system.

items.title: First-principles channel model and capacity-achieving transmission scheme in thermal noise backscatter links
items.summary_raw: Thermal noise communication systems transmit information by modulating thermal radiation, eliminating the need for a dedicated signal power source and making them attractive solutions for low-power sensor networks. Their efficiency enables long-lived, unobtrusive operation, which is valuable in the Internet of Things, electromagnetic interference-sensitive environments, and radio frequency identification tag systems. However, a limited understanding of the wireless channel model and efficient transmission schemes has hindered their practical deployment. Here, we present a wireless channel model that elucidates how systems operating at ambient temperature can modulate thermal noise to convey information. Our results reveal a thermal noise backscatter mechanism that enables significantly higher data rates than previously achieved. We designed and built a thermal noise communication system leveraging this mechanism to achieve data rates in the kilobits-per-second range—over two orders of magnitude higher than prior demonstrations. We also derive the system capacity and show that using polar codes, we are able to achieve this expected capacity. Our channel model and transmission scheme pave the way for strategies in thermal noise sensing and communication, advancing practical low-power networking for next-generation wireless applications.

items.title: Lhx9 specifically modulates phalanx number, whereas Lhx2 constrains digit length in tetrapods
items.summary_raw: Most nonmammalian tetrapods exhibit more than three phalanges in their posterior digits (III–V), whereas mammals are restricted to no more than three. So far, the molecular mechanism underlying this evolutionary reduction and the functions of Lhx2 and Lhx9 in digit development remain unclear. Here we show divergent evolution of Lhx2 and Lhx9 expression patterns in embryonic limbs across tetrapods. We further demonstrate that although ectopic overexpression of each gene in chick embryos delayed limb skeletal development, only Lhx9 reduced the phalanx number in the posterior digits. Transcriptomic analysis showed that Lhx2 regulates pathways for chondrocyte and osteoblast differentiation, and Lhx9 preferentially influences skeletal segmentation via the bone morphogenetic protein (BMP) pathway. The unique function and differential expression of Lhx9 in the limb buds between mammals and nonmammalian tetrapods suggest it may have acquired a role in suppressing phalanx number, driving the evolutionary reduction of phalanx number in mammals.

items.title: PLD1-driven oncogenic secretion creates a therapeutic vulnerability in chromosome 3q–amplified NSCLC
items.summary_raw: Chromosome 3q (3q) amplification is a frequent event in non–small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) and other cancer types, yet therapeutic strategies targeting oncogenic drivers within this amplicon have been unsuccessful. Our study revealed that the 3q amplicon encodes multiple Golgi-related proteins, including Phospholipase D1 (PLD1), which catalyzes the production of a potential oncogenic lipid, phosphatidic acid. We found that PLD1 is highly expressed in 3q-amplified NSCLC (3q-NSCLC) and its enzymatic activity is further boosted by coamplified PLD1 activator, ARF-like GTPase 14. High PLD1 activity is essential for 3q-NSCLC growth and metastasis. Mechanistically, PLD1 drives secretion of oncogenic factors via the carriers from the trans Golgi network to the cell surface pathway to support tumor growth. Transferrin receptor 1 (TFRC), which encodes a membrane protein, is coamplified with PLD1 and overexpressed in 3q-NSCLC. A TFRC antibody–drug conjugate (ADC) carrying a PLD1 inhibitor exhibited potential antitumor activity in mouse models. These findings establish PLD1 as a promoter of 3q-NSCLC and provide proof of concept for the development of PLD1-targeted therapies, including ADC-based approaches, for this challenging cancer subtype.

items.title: Diminishing cooling returns of urban greening amid a warming climate
items.summary_raw: Urban greening is widely prioritized as a nature-based solution to mitigating intensifying heat extremes in the context of climate change, yet its long-term global efficacy remains inadequately quantified. Here we present a two-decade assessment of vegetation dynamics and associated cooling effects across 3,806 urban clusters worldwide, integrating multisource satellite observations with ground measurements from 4,855 meteorological stations. We identify a pronounced climate equity gap: While cities in the Global North have largely expanded green infrastructure, they exhibit cooling saturation with diminishing biophysical returns. Conversely, most cities in the Global South show vegetation stagnation or loss, compounding rapid warming trends. This asymmetry exposes a critical climate justice challenge, indicating that current greening efforts are insufficient to offset a warming trend. Our findings underscore the necessity for context-specific, integrated climate adaptation frameworks that address both the quantity and quality of urban vegetation to achieve equitable thermal resilience in an increasingly warm world.

items.title: The susceptibility to weight gain in male C57BL/6 mice fed high-fat diet is due to a small set of genes predominantly not expressed in the brain
items.summary_raw: Obesity results from a gene by environment interaction. Understanding the impacts of environmental factors like diet on body weight/fatness has been greatly facilitated by rodent models. We previously identified the responses of males of five mouse strains fed 30 different diets. Two of these strains showed much greater weight gain and two were resistant. Sixty-six marker SNPs in 57 genes were identified, which have a genetic motif across the four strains reflecting their protection or susceptibility to high-fat diet (HFD). We used two of these strains: C57BL/6 and BALB/c, in a classic approach of cross-breeding the strains, to generate a F1 generation, and then cross-breeding their offspring to generate an F2 population. The F2 males were fed HFD and phenotyped for body weight, fat mass, and energy intake and genotyped for the 66 SNPs. Body mass gain on HFD was influenced by 17 SNPs in 11 genes explaining 87% of the individual variation in weight gain. We then measured gene expression of these 11 genes in 16 tissues of male and female C57BL/6 and Balb/c mice when fed high- or low-fat diets, and in 6 tissues of mice exposed to different levels of calorie restriction, to map their expression profiles. The genes were widely expressed in a diversity of tissues including several not normally suspected to be important for fat storage regulation (e.g., testis, lungs, and spleen) with only four expressed predominantly in the hypothalamus. Body fat regulation is probably more…

items.title: Heterogeneous amyloid β dimerization revealed by single-molecule FRET and MD simulation
items.summary_raw: The correlation between specific amyloid fibril polymorphs and diseases suggests that characterization of heterogeneity in the aggregation process is key to understanding disease mechanisms. In this work, we use single-molecule Förster resonance energy transfer (FRET) spectroscopy and molecular dynamics (MD) simulation to quantitatively characterize dimerization of amyloid β (Aβ), the first step of the aggregation process. We find that dimerization is extremely rare, with a high dissociation constant of >16 mM, yet there are multiple dimer states with distinct FRET efficiencies and stabilities, many of which survive for milliseconds to seconds. The dimer population increases with the increasing ionic strength and decreasing pH, indicating the importance of nonspecific electrostatic interactions in dimer formation. MD simulations with enhanced sampling demonstrate the formation of diverse bound states having a range of FRET efficiencies and flexible N termini, compatible with the experimental observations. There are conformational clusters represented by the formation of three mixed parallel/antiparallel β strands forming Greek key-like motifs and the formation of antiparallel β strands, which may be representative of dimers with longer and shorter lifetimes, respectively, observed in the FRET experiment. items.title: Ecological, physiological, and evolutionary drivers of stoichiometry in insects
items.summary_raw: The elemental composition of organisms links physiology to biogeochemical cycles, yet the relative contributions of evolutionary divergence, ecology, and allometry to stoichiometric variation remain incompletely resolved. Here, we integrate a global insect stoichiometric database spanning 223 species with a comprehensive phylogenetic backbone to evaluate the relative importance of hypothesized ecophysiological drivers of carbon (C), nitrogen (N), and phosphorus (P) stoichiometry within a multivariate framework. We found a strong phylogenetic signal in stoichiometric ratios and in P and N content, with evolutionary divergence (phylogenetic structure) accounting for approximately half of the explained variation in P-based ratios, exceeding the contribution of any individual ecological predictor. Phylogenetically corrected models recover trophic enrichment across successive trophic levels, consistent with previously documented patterns, and positive scaling between body mass and both C:P and N:P, in line with the general predictions of the Growth Rate Hypothesis. Temperature was the strongest ecological predictor of insect stoichiometry, with positive effects on C:P and N:P ratios and a negative effect on C:N, highlighting the thermal underpinnings of previously observed geographic patterns. items.title: Climate Refugee Responsibility Sharing and Protection Pathways
items.source_name: Lecture Notes in Education Psychology and Public Media
items.summary_raw: The Australia–Tuvalu Falepili Union represents one of the few existing attempts to create a legal pathway for people affected by climate change. Its limited reach, however, reveals the broader limitations of the current international legal framework. Under the existing refugee regime, persons displaced by sea-level rise, environmental degradation, and climate-related disasters still lack a clearly recognized legal status. This article examines the legal challenges surrounding climate refugee protection through an analysis of international refugee law, human rights-based protection practices, and emerging regional arrangements. It argues that the core difficulty lies not only in recognizing climate-displaced persons, but also in establishing a fair and effective system of responsibility allocation. Based on the principle of common but differentiated responsibilities, this article proposes that developed countries should undertake greater obligations in financing, technology transfer, and settlement assistance, while regional and domestic mechanisms may provide supplementary protection. Although arrangements such as the Falepili Union offer valuable practical experience, they cannot replace broader international legal reform. A future protection framework should therefore integrate legal status recognition, responsibility-sharing mechanisms, and coordinated protection pathways to address the growing challenges of climate-induced displacement.

It further requires the state to take reasonable measures to prevent environmental degradation, protect natural resources, and promote sustainable development. Despite this constitutional commitment, South Africa continues to experience increasing climate risks and environmental challenges. Small businesses, particularly those operating in informal and urban settings, are both contributors to and affected by these challenges. Their activities may contribute to environmental harm through poor waste management, inefficient energy use, and limited access to sustainable practices. At the same time, they remain vulnerable to climate impacts such as flooding, water shortages, and extreme weather events. This study examines how weaknesses in climate policy implementation undermine the practical realization of environmental rights under section 24. Using qualitative doctrinal and policy analysis, the study evaluates constitutional provisions, environmental legislation, climate policies, and governance frameworks. items.title: Public support for a carbon tax towards cleaner-energy transition: an experimental investigation
items.summary_raw: Abstract People worldwide aim to reduce the adverse impacts from carbon emissions by adopting clean energy sources. Hitherto, few studies have investigated how these policies can be concretely designed to facilitate cleaner-energy transition. We pose a question of how a carbon tax can be an effective instrument at transitioning to clean energy and hypothesize that information provision can influence people’s support to the tax. We experimentally examine the determinants influencing public support for the introduction of the carbon tax via a vignette experiment with 1500 Japanese subjects. The vignette policy dimensions include “who pays the tax,” “how the tax gets paid,” “where the revenue gets used” and “how much the burden becomes,” each introduced as a treatment with the baseline of no information. Results indicate that public support comparatively increases when the entities specified to pay are producers, when the tax revenue is used towards renewable energies and when the burden is sufficiently low. Overall, we demonstrate that a carbon tax can be an effective policy instrument for cleaner-energy transition, while garnering public support and ample revenue. It is recommended that the carbon-tax policy design targets producers and renewable energy along with a per-capita burden between 500 JPY and 3000 JPY a month.

items.title: Research on the evolutionary characteristics of hot topics in online public opinion of Chinese universities based on Weibo texts
items.summary_raw: Investigating the evolutionary characteristics of hot topics in the online public opinion of Chinese universities contributes to the identification and prediction of trends in university-related public opinion, offering valuable insights for the management of public discourse. This study collected and processed hot search data related to universities from Weibo between 2020 and 2024. The data were analyzed for topic discovery and sentiment using the LDA and BERT models. The evolutionary characteristics of these hot topics were then examined through data visualization. The results revealed that, over the past 5 years, the main topics in online public opinion related to Chinese universities fell into seven categories: Female faculty and students, Graduation and employment, Campus management and security, Education and teaching, Illegal activities and violations, Campus life, and Examination and enrollment. The evolution of these topics displayed distinct patterns: cyclical fluctuations in both the quantity and sentiment of education-related public opinion, the generation of topics driven by unforeseen events, shifts in hot topics influenced by educational values, and the polarization of sentiment surrounding these topics driven by online debates. This paper presents a research methodology for studying the evolution of university public opinion topics and provides a reference for understanding and managing public opinion in Chinese universities.

items.title: Managing The Organizational Climate in The Digital Era for Teachers at SMP Negeri 4 Pakem and SMP Binajaya Banguntapan
items.summary_raw: This study aimed to analyze organizational climate management in the digital era for teachers at SMP Negeri 4 Pakem and SMP Bina Jaya Banguntapan and to identify the supporting and inhibiting factors affecting its implementation. The study employed a qualitative approach using a case study design and was conducted at two schools with distinct organizational climate characteristics. The participants included the school principals and ten teachers, comprising five teachers from SMP Negeri 4 Pakem and five teachers from SMP Bina Jaya Banguntapan. The study focused on teachers' attitudes and behaviors in their interactions with school principals and colleagues. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews, structured observations using observation sheets, and document analysis. The trustworthiness of the data was assessed based on credibility, transferability, dependability, and confirmability, supported by methodological, source, and temporal triangulation. Data were analyzed using the Miles and Huberman interactive model. The findings indicated that organizational climate management in the digital era was implemented through five management functions: planning, organizing, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation. Supporting factors included the enhancement of teachers' digital competencies through training and professional learning communities, principals' transformational leadership, and school policies supporting the provision of cloud-based databases, a basic…

items.title: Directed assembly of cathode interlayers enables efficient binary organic solar cells
items.summary_raw: Abstract Cathode interlayers create interfacial dipoles in organic solar cells to maximize device efficiency. However, the dipoles are highly dependent on the molecular orientation of the interlayers, which remain challenging to be controlled. Here, based on the amphiphilic nature of the interlayers, we show a stepwise film deposition approach using a polar solvent for active layer pretreatment and a bipolar solvent for subsequent interlayer self assembly. Sum-frequency generation vibrational spectroscopy reveals a preferred perpendicular orientation of the interlayer molecules, thereby enhancing the surface potential and reducing the charge transport resistance. As a result, we achieve a certified efficiency of 20.65% and fill factor of 82.7% in binary organic solar cells. This method is universally applicable to different cathode interlayers and active layers. Our work highlights the importance of controlling interlayer molecular orientation for unlocking significant performance gains, paving the way for further advancements in device optimization.

items.title: Gendered Performance Inequities Rooted in Assessment Design and Educational Climate in Vocational and Technical Education
items.summary_raw: Gender-neutral assessment and evaluation procedures contribute to gender discrepancies in vocational and technical education. Previous studies have primarily examined aspects in isolation, resulting in a disjointed understanding of their interconnections. This study aims to outline the expressions and sources of gender bias in assessment and evaluation within vocational and technical education. This study utilizes a systematic evaluation of vocational and technical education, conforming to PRISMA 2020 principles, and examines Scopus, Taylor & Francis Online, IEEE Xplore, and ScienceDirect from 2023 to 2025 via quality screening, bibliometric analysis (VOSviewer), and thematic synthesis. An examination of 68 studies revealed five interrelated types of bias in vocational education assessment and evaluation practices: structural assessment design bias, educational climate factors, vocational education certification-accreditation bias, vocational education competency assessment bias, and pedagogical framework bias. These biases emerge from the interaction of psychological factors (test anxiety, stereotype threat, self-efficacy), instructional design (high-stakes timed assessments, restrictive rubrics), and institutional conditions (assessment norms/policies), suggesting that bias is a product of multi-level interactions rather than a single variable.

Political Allusions in Philippine News Media: Framing, Rhetoric, and Democratic Discourse
items.source_name: International Journal of Research on Multidisciplinary Studies
items.summary_raw: Political allusions provide culturally and historically resonant references through which political issues and actors may be represented in news discourse. Despite their presence in Philippine political communication, their forms and rhetorical and framing functions remain insufficiently examined in local media scholarship. This study examined the types, framing functions, and rhetorical functions of political allusions in Philippine political media discourse. A qualitative Critical Discourse Analysis was conducted on 50 purposively selected political media articles published between 2024 and 2025 by ABS-CBN, Philippine Daily Inquirer, Manila Bulletin, The Philippine Star, and Rappler. The analysis classified political allusions according to their historical, mythological, religious, literary, and popular-cultural references and examined their association with hero, villain, and victim frames and with Aristotelian rhetorical appeals of ethos, pathos, and logos. Historical allusions were the most frequently identified, with 22 instances, followed by popular-cultural allusions (13), literary allusions (9), religious allusions (5), and mythological allusions (1). Villain framing was the most prevalent framing pattern (38 instances), followed by hero (7) and victim (5) frames. Pathos was the most frequently identified rhetorical function (40 instances), while ethos and logos each accounted for five. The findings indicate that political allusions in the selected articles…

Water Consumption and Hydration Status in Children Living in Hot Climate Conditions
items.summary_raw: Adequate hydration is essential for maintaining physiological homeostasis, thermoregulation, and cognitive performance in children. Children are particularly vulnerable to dehydration due to physiological characteristics and behavioral factors, especially in hot climate conditions. This review aims to summarize current evidence regarding water consumption patterns, hydration status, and health outcomes associated with inadequate hydration in children living in hot climate environments. This study was conducted as a narrative review. A structured literature search was performed using electronic databases including PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science. Studies evaluating hydration status, water intake, and related health outcomes in pediatric populations were included, and the findings were qualitatively synthesized. Available evidence indicates that a substantial proportion of children do not meet recommended daily water intake levels and frequently experience mild underhydration. Water consumption is often replaced by sugar-sweetened beverages, and environmental factors such as school settings and limited access to drinking water may further contribute to inadequate intake. Heat exposure significantly increases fluid loss and the risk of dehydration, which may lead to adverse health outcomes including electrolyte imbalance, renal stress, and heat-related illnesses. Hydration status is commonly assessed using biomarkers such as urine osmolality and urine specific gravity…

items.title: Implementation Models and Barriers for Residential Building Energy Retrofits
items.summary_raw: In the process of long-term use, existing residences are prone to problems such as the decline in the performance of the enclosure structure, the ageing of the equipment and the reduction of energy utilisation efficiency. Energy-saving transformation can reduce the energy consumption of the building to a certain extent and improve the living environment. However, factors such as the dispersion of residential property rights, high early investment, differences in residents' needs and later maintenance make the transformation project face more difficulties in the actual promotion. This paper adopts the methods of literature induction and typical case analysis to analyse the three implementation models of energy-saving transformation of residential buildings: contract energy management, government-led and comprehensive services, and compare their funding sources, subject division of labour, risk bearing and project organisation methods. The analysis found that contract energy management helps to alleviate the early capital pressure. The government-led model has certain advantages in policy support and multi-subject coordination, while the comprehensive service model pays more attention to the connection between different participants and implementation links. The actual effect of different models is affected by factors such as fund recovery, resident participation, organisational coordination and long-term operation and maintenance. The selection of the implementation model of…

items.title: Climate change knowledge, attitudes, and practices among future physicians in Egypt
items.summary_raw: Climate change poses significant threats to public health, necessitating proactive engagement from healthcare professionals. However, there is limited research on the knowledge, attitudes, and practices of future physicians in Egypt regarding climate change and health. This study aims to fill this gap and generate insights that can guide institutional reforms and policy development. A cross-sectional study was conducted between June and November 2024, involving 797 medical students and interns from 34 Egyptian medical schools. Data were collected using convenience sampling via an online anonymous questionnaire, covering sociodemographics, climate change knowledge, attitudes, and practices. Most participants (94.3%) were aware of climate change. However, knowledge of indirect health impacts, such as links to social inequality (52.7%) and reproductive health (45%), was limited. The primary sources of climate change information were the internet (87.8%) and social media (86.2%), and 74.5% of participants agreed that climate change should be included in medical curricula. Students exposed to climate change content in their curriculum demonstrated significantly higher personal mitigation and advocacy practices scores compared to their peers (both p < .05). While 69.9% believed physicians should raise awareness, only 30% reported encouraging climate-related local policies. Most of the participating medical students were aware of climate change but lacked comprehensive knowledge of…

items.title: Framing the unknowable: The role of language and frame multiplicity in early‐stage startup pitches
items.summary_raw: Abstract Research Summary Early‐stage startup pitches must make largely unknowable futures plausible. As such, they bear a rhetorical burden. This study theorizes how multiple frames jointly shape this burden and, consequently, affect investor evaluations. Specifically, it considers how future growth frames interact with concreteness and novelty frames. Evidence from 618 startup pitches and ad‐hoc investor evaluations reveals that growth frames relying more on entrepreneurs' own assertions than on established grounds tend to receive lower investor evaluations. This evaluative discount is alleviated when growth is expressed concretely but becomes more pronounced when the pitch emphasizes novelty. These findings extend framing theory by explaining the relevance and possible implications of frame multiplicity in pitches and entrepreneurial communication more broadly. Managerial Summary Mobilizing support for a new venture is difficult because founders must often describe a future that does not yet exist. This study of 618 startup pitches shows that growth‐related messages can shape investor evaluations even at the earliest stage, but only if configured well. Because growth frames must appear plausible amid the uncertainty surrounding new startups, framing early‐stage startups around growth is rhetorically burdensome. Findings show that pitches are evaluated less favorably when they rely more on founders' own projections and reasoning than on established grounds such as market…

items.title: Understanding and reducing methane emissions: insights into anthropogenic, natural sources, and novel mitigation techniques
items.summary_raw: Abstract Methane (CH 4 ) is a potent, short-lived greenhouse gas. Among the major well-mixed greenhouse gases, it ranks second only to carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) in its contribution to anthropogenic radiative forcing. Although methane remains in the atmosphere for approximately 12 years, its 100-year global warming potential (GWP100) is approximately 27–30 times greater than that of CO 2 (IPCC AR6), making rapid mitigation a critical near-term climate strategy. This review synthesizes current understanding of methane emissions from anthropogenic and natural sources, evaluates sector-specific mitigation potentials, and critically examines emerging reduction technologies. Fossil fuel extraction, agriculture (particularly enteric fermentation), and waste management collectively account for the majority of anthropogenic methane emissions, with significant variability in mitigation feasibility and cost-effectiveness. Advanced methane monitoring systems, feed additives, biochar applications, leak detection technologies, and microbial interventions show considerable mitigation potential but face technical limitations, high implementation costs, infrastructure barriers, and scalability challenges. We emphasize sectoral prioritization, policy integration, and trade-offs associated with mitigation strategies. Immediate methane reductions offer substantial co-benefits, including improved air quality and public health, while directly supporting Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs 13, 7, and…
